<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation">ElevenLabs API Documentation v1.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

This is the documentation for the ElevenLabs API. You can use this API to use our service programmatically, this is done by using your API key. You can find your API key in the dashboard at https://elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys.

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-text-to-speech">text-to-speech</h1>

Convert text into lifelike speech using a voice of your choice.

## Text To Speech

<a id="opIdtext_to_speech_full"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "text": "This is a test for the API of ElevenLabs.",
    "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_v2",
    "language_code": "en",
    "voice_settings": {
      "similarity_boost": 1,
      "speed": 1,
      "stability": 1,
      "style": 0,
      "use_speaker_boost": true
    },
    "pronunciation_dictionary_locators": [
      {
        "pronunciation_dictionary_id": "test",
        "version_id": "id2"
      }
    ],
    "seed": 12345,
    "previous_text": "In the heart of a lush valley surrounded by towering mountains lies the quaint village of Willowbrook.",
    "next_text": "The Willowbrook Festival, held every spring, celebrates the blossoming of the wild bluebells that carpet the nearby forest floors, creating a breathtaking sea of blue under the canopy of fresh green leaves.",
    "previous_request_ids": [
      "09bOJkdYVjKy2oOiiVtR",
      "0p2uKqOnZyce22SPZ9d5",
      "1KYvY8WZAKmcjCJ1mvVB"
    ],
    "next_request_ids": [
      "3tPgBrD1UdW3snUkGw1K",
      "4D1jAxiRFkolBNUGzXkU",
      "4c8Z4aWliVR2oipYRXhj"
    ],
    "use_pvc_as_ivc": true,
    "apply_text_normalization": true,
    "apply_language_text_normalization": true,
    "audio_effects": {
      "filter_preset_id": "string",
      "distance": 0,
      "environment_id": "string",
      "background_noise_id": "string",
      "send_level": 1,
      "pan": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}`

Converts text into speech using a voice of your choice and returns audio.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text": "This is a test for the API of ElevenLabs.",
  "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_v2",
  "language_code": "en",
  "voice_settings": {
    "similarity_boost": 1,
    "speed": 1,
    "stability": 1,
    "style": 0,
    "use_speaker_boost": true
  },
  "pronunciation_dictionary_locators": [
    {
      "pronunciation_dictionary_id": "test",
      "version_id": "id2"
    }
  ],
  "seed": 12345,
  "previous_text": "In the heart of a lush valley surrounded by towering mountains lies the quaint village of Willowbrook.",
  "next_text": "The Willowbrook Festival, held every spring, celebrates the blossoming of the wild bluebells that carpet the nearby forest floors, creating a breathtaking sea of blue under the canopy of fresh green leaves.",
  "previous_request_ids": [
    "09bOJkdYVjKy2oOiiVtR",
    "0p2uKqOnZyce22SPZ9d5",
    "1KYvY8WZAKmcjCJ1mvVB"
  ],
  "next_request_ids": [
    "3tPgBrD1UdW3snUkGw1K",
    "4D1jAxiRFkolBNUGzXkU",
    "4c8Z4aWliVR2oipYRXhj"
  ],
  "use_pvc_as_ivc": true,
  "apply_text_normalization": true,
  "apply_language_text_normalization": true,
  "audio_effects": {
    "filter_preset_id": "string",
    "distance": 0,
    "environment_id": "string",
    "background_noise_id": "string",
    "send_level": 1,
    "pan": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="text-to-speech-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice_id|path|string|true|Voice ID to be used, you can use https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices to list all the available voices.|
|enable_logging|query|boolean|false|When enable_logging is set to false zero retention mode will be used for the request. This will mean history features are unavailable for this request, including request stitching. Zero retention mode may only be used by enterprise customers.|
|optimize_streaming_latency|query|integer \| null|false|**Deprecated.** You can turn on latency optimizations at some cost of quality. The best possible final latency varies by model. Possible values:<br>0 - default mode (no latency optimizations)<br>1 - normal latency optimizations (about 50% of possible latency improvement of option 3)<br>2 - strong latency optimizations (about 75% of possible latency improvement of option 3)<br>3 - max latency optimizations<br>4 - max latency optimizations, but also with text normalizer turned off for even more latency savings (best latency, but can mispronounce eg numbers and dates).<br><br>Defaults to None.<br>|
|output_format|query|string|false|Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM and WAV formats with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_text_to_speech_full](#schemabody_text_to_speech_full)|true|none|
|» text|body|string|true|The text that will get converted into speech.|
|» model_id|body|string|false|Identifier of the model that will be used, you can query them using GET /v1/models. The model needs to have support for text to speech, you can check this using the can_do_text_to_speech property.|
|» language_code|body|string \| null|false|Language code (ISO 639-1) used to enforce a language for the model and text normalization. If the model does not support the provided language code, it will be ignored. This parameter is not supported for multilingual_v2 models.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» voice_settings|body|[VoiceSettingsResponseModel](#schemavoicesettingsresponsemodel) \| null|false|Voice settings overriding stored settings for the given voice. They are applied only on the given request.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[VoiceSettingsResponseModel](#schemavoicesettingsresponsemodel)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» pronunciation_dictionary_locators|body|[[PronunciationDictionaryVersionLocatorRequestModel](#schemapronunciationdictionaryversionlocatorrequestmodel)] \| null|false|A list of pronunciation dictionary locators (id, version_id) to be applied to the text. They will be applied in order. You may have up to 3 locators per request|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[[PronunciationDictionaryVersionLocatorRequestModel](#schemapronunciationdictionaryversionlocatorrequestmodel)]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» seed|body|integer \| null|false|If specified, our system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should return the same result. Determinism is not guaranteed. Must be integer between 0 and 4294967295.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» previous_text|body|string \| null|false|The text that came before the text of the current request. Can be used to improve the speech's continuity when concatenating together multiple generations or to influence the speech's continuity in the current generation.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» next_text|body|string \| null|false|The text that comes after the text of the current request. Can be used to improve the speech's continuity when concatenating together multiple generations or to influence the speech's continuity in the current generation.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» previous_request_ids|body|[string] \| null|false|A list of request_id of the samples that were generated before this generation. Can be used to improve the speech's continuity when splitting up a large task into multiple requests. The results will be best when the same model is used across the generations. In case both previous_text and previous_request_ids is send, previous_text will be ignored. A maximum of 3 request_ids can be send.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» next_request_ids|body|[string] \| null|false|A list of request_id of the samples that come after this generation. next_request_ids is especially useful for maintaining the speech's continuity when regenerating a sample that has had some audio quality issues. For example, if you have generated 3 speech clips, and you want to improve clip 2, passing the request id of clip 3 as a next_request_id (and that of clip 1 as a previous_request_id) will help maintain natural flow in the combined speech. The results will be best when the same model is used across the generations. In case both next_text and next_request_ids is send, next_text will be ignored. A maximum of 3 request_ids can be send.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» use_pvc_as_ivc|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to use the IVC version of a professional voice. This may improve expressiveness and reduce latency.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» apply_text_normalization|body|string|false|This parameter controls text normalization with three modes: 'auto', 'on', and 'off'. When set to 'auto', the system will automatically decide whether to apply text normalization (e.g., spelling out numbers). With 'on', text normalization will always be applied, while with 'off', it will be skipped.|
|» apply_language_text_normalization|body|boolean|false|This parameter controls language text normalization. This helps with proper pronunciation of text in some supported languages. WARNING: This parameter can heavily increase the latency of the request. Currently only supported for Japanese.|
|» audio_effects|body|[EffectsSpec-Input](#schemaeffectsspec-input) \| null|false|Audio effects applied to the generated audio. Unknown IDs return 404 with `param` naming the field. Reverb (`environment_id` with `send_level` above 0) and a non-zero `pan` produce stereo audio and are rejected with 400 for `ulaw_*`, `alaw_*`, and `pcm_*` output formats. Effects don't change the cost of the request.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[EffectsSpec-Input](#schemaeffectsspec-input)|false|Audio effects applied to generated speech: a filter preset, perceived distance, a reverb<br>environment, a background noise bed, and stereo panning. Leave every field at its default<br>to get unprocessed audio.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

|» apply_text_normalization|auto|

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The generated audio file|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

`POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/with-timestamps`

## Text To Speech Streaming

<a id="opIdtext_to_speech_stream"></a>

> Code samples

`POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream`

Converts text into speech using a voice of your choice and returns audio as an audio stream.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text": "This is a test for the API of ElevenLabs.",
  "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_v2",
  "language_code": "en",
  "voice_settings": {
    "similarity_boost": 1,
    "speed": 1,
    "stability": 1,
    "style": 0,
    "use_speaker_boost": true
  },
  "pronunciation_dictionary_locators": [
    {
      "pronunciation_dictionary_id": "test",
      "version_id": "id2"
    }
  ],
  "seed": 12345,
  "previous_text": "In the heart of a lush valley surrounded by towering mountains lies the quaint village of Willowbrook.",
  "next_text": "The Willowbrook Festival, held every spring, celebrates the blossoming of the wild bluebells that carpet the nearby forest floors, creating a breathtaking sea of blue under the canopy of fresh green leaves.",
  "previous_request_ids": [
    "09bOJkdYVjKy2oOiiVtR",
    "0p2uKqOnZyce22SPZ9d5",
    "1KYvY8WZAKmcjCJ1mvVB"
  ],
  "next_request_ids": [
    "3tPgBrD1UdW3snUkGw1K",
    "4D1jAxiRFkolBNUGzXkU",
    "4c8Z4aWliVR2oipYRXhj"
  ],
  "use_pvc_as_ivc": true,
  "apply_text_normalization": true,
  "apply_language_text_normalization": true,
  "audio_effects": {
    "filter_preset_id": "string",

    "background_noise_id": "string",
    "send_level": 1,
    "pan": 0
  }
}

<h3 id="text-to-speech-streaming-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice_id|path|string|true|Voice ID to be used, you can use https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices to list all the available voices.|
|enable_logging|query|boolean|false|When enable_logging is set to false zero retention mode will be used for the request. This will mean history features are unavailable for this request, including request stitching. Zero retention mode may only be used by enterprise customers.|
|optimize_streaming_latency|query|integer \| null|false|**Deprecated.** You can turn on latency optimizations at some cost of quality. The best possible final latency varies by model. Possible values:<br>0 - default mode (no latency optimizations)<br>1 - normal latency optimizations (about 50% of possible latency improvement of option 3)<br>2 - strong latency optimizations (about 75% of possible latency improvement of option 3)<br>3 - max latency optimizations<br>4 - max latency optimizations, but also with text normalizer turned off for even more latency savings (best latency, but can mispronounce eg numbers and dates).<br><br>Defaults to None.<br>|
|output_format|query|string|false|Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_text_to_speech_stream](#schemabody_text_to_speech_stream)|true|none|
|» text|body|string|true|The text that will get converted into speech.|
|» model_id|body|string|false|Identifier of the model that will be used, you can query them using GET /v1/models. The model needs to have support for text to speech, you can check this using the can_do_text_to_speech property.|
|» language_code|body|string \| null|false|Language code (ISO 639-1) used to enforce a language for the model and text normalization. If the model does not support the provided language code, it will be ignored. This parameter is not supported for multilingual_v2 models.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» voice_settings|body|[VoiceSettingsResponseModel](#schemavoicesettingsresponsemodel) \| null|false|Voice settings overriding stored settings for the given voice. They are applied only on the given request.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[VoiceSettingsResponseModel](#schemavoicesettingsresponsemodel)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» pronunciation_dictionary_locators|body|[[PronunciationDictionaryVersionLocatorRequestModel](#schemapronunciationdictionaryversionlocatorrequestmodel)] \| null|false|A list of pronunciation dictionary locators (id, version_id) to be applied to the text. They will be applied in order. You may have up to 3 locators per request|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[[PronunciationDictionaryVersionLocatorRequestModel](#schemapronunciationdictionaryversionlocatorrequestmodel)]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» seed|body|integer \| null|false|If specified, our system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should return the same result. Determinism is not guaranteed. Must be integer between 0 and 4294967295.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» previous_text|body|string \| null|false|The text that came before the text of the current request. Can be used to improve the speech's continuity when concatenating together multiple generations or to influence the speech's continuity in the current generation.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» next_text|body|string \| null|false|The text that comes after the text of the current request. Can be used to improve the speech's continuity when concatenating together multiple generations or to influence the speech's continuity in the current generation.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» previous_request_ids|body|[string] \| null|false|A list of request_id of the samples that were generated before this generation. Can be used to improve the speech's continuity when splitting up a large task into multiple requests. The results will be best when the same model is used across the generations. In case both previous_text and previous_request_ids is send, previous_text will be ignored. A maximum of 3 request_ids can be send.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» next_request_ids|body|[string] \| null|false|A list of request_id of the samples that come after this generation. next_request_ids is especially useful for maintaining the speech's continuity when regenerating a sample that has had some audio quality issues. For example, if you have generated 3 speech clips, and you want to improve clip 2, passing the request id of clip 3 as a next_request_id (and that of clip 1 as a previous_request_id) will help maintain natural flow in the combined speech. The results will be best when the same model is used across the generations. In case both next_text and next_request_ids is send, next_text will be ignored. A maximum of 3 request_ids can be send.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» use_pvc_as_ivc|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to use the IVC version of a professional voice. This may improve expressiveness and reduce latency.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» apply_text_normalization|body|string|false|This parameter controls text normalization with three modes: 'auto', 'on', and 'off'. When set to 'auto', the system will automatically decide whether to apply text normalization (e.g., spelling out numbers). With 'on', text normalization will always be applied, while with 'off', it will be skipped.|
|» apply_language_text_normalization|body|boolean|false|This parameter controls language text normalization. This helps with proper pronunciation of text in some supported languages. WARNING: This parameter can heavily increase the latency of the request. Currently only supported for Japanese.|
|» audio_effects|body|[EffectsSpec-Input](#schemaeffectsspec-input) \| null|false|Audio effects applied to the generated audio. Unknown IDs return 404 with `param` naming the field. Reverb (`environment_id` with `send_level` above 0) and a non-zero `pan` produce stereo audio and are rejected with 400 for `ulaw_*`, `alaw_*`, and `pcm_*` output formats. Effects don't change the cost of the request.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[EffectsSpec-Input](#schemaeffectsspec-input)|false|Audio effects applied to generated speech: a filter preset, perceived distance, a reverb<br>environment, a background noise bed, and stereo panning. Leave every field at its default<br>to get unprocessed audio.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-voice-changer">voice-changer</h1>

Transform audio from one voice to another, keeping its emotion, timing and delivery.

## Voice Changer

<a id="opIdspeech_to_speech_full"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voice-changer/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'audio=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'model_id=eleven_english_sts_v2' \
  -F 'voice_settings=string' \
  -F 'seed=12345' \
  -F 'remove_background_noise=true' \
  -F 'file_format=pcm_s16le_16'
```

`POST /v1/voice-changer/{voice_id}`

Transform audio from one voice to another. Maintain full control over emotion, timing and delivery.

> Body parameter

```yaml
audio: string
model_id: eleven_english_sts_v2
voice_settings: string
seed: 12345

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-speech-to-text">speech-to-text</h1>

Transcribe your audio files with detailed speaker annotations and precise timestamps using our cutting-edge model.

## Speech To Text

<a id="opIdspeech_to_text"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/speech-to-text \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'model_id=scribe_v2' \
  -F 'file=string' \
  -F 'language_code=string' \
  -F 'transcript_edit=string' \
  -F 'tag_audio_events=true' \
  -F 'num_speakers=1' \
  -F 'timestamps_granularity=word' \
  -F 'diarize=false' \
  -F 'diarization_threshold=0.1' \
  -F 'additional_formats=[{"include_speakers":true,"include_timestamps":true,"format":"segmented_json","segment_on_silence_longer_than_s":0,"max_segment_duration_s":0,"max_segment_chars":0}]' \
  -F 'file_format=pcm_s16le_16' \
  -F 'cloud_storage_url=https://storage.googleapis.com/my-bucket/folder/audio.mp3' \
  -F 'source_url=https://storage.googleapis.com/my-bucket/folder/audio.mp3' \
  -F 'webhook=false' \
  -F 'webhook_id=string' \
  -F 'temperature=0' \
  -F 'seed=12345' \
  -F 'use_multi_channel=false' \
  -F 'multichannel_output_style=separate' \
  -F 'webhook_metadata={"user_id": "123", "session_id": "abc-def-ghi"}' \
  -F 'entity_detection=string' \
  -F 'no_verbatim=false' \
  -F 'use_speaker_library=false' \
  -F 'detect_speaker_roles=false' \
  -F 'entity_redaction=string' \
  -F 'entity_redaction_mode=enumerated_entity_type' \
  -F 'keyterms=[]'
```

`POST /v1/speech-to-text`

Transcribe an audio or video file. If webhook is set to true, the request will be processed asynchronously and results sent to configured webhooks. When use_multi_channel is true and the provided audio has multiple channels, a 'transcripts' object with separate transcripts for each channel is returned; set multichannel_output_style='combined' to instead receive a single transcript with all channels merged and sorted by time. Otherwise, returns a single transcript. The optional webhook_metadata parameter allows you to attach custom data that will be included in webhook responses for request correlation and tracking.

> Body parameter

```yaml
model_id: scribe_v2
file: string
language_code: string
transcript_edit: string
tag_audio_events: true
num_speakers: 1
timestamps_granularity: word
diarize: false
diarization_threshold: 0.1
additional_formats:
  -
    include_speakers: true
    include_timestamps: true
    format: segmented_json
    segment_on_silence_longer_than_s: 0
    max_segment_duration_s: 0
    max_segment_chars: 0
file_format: pcm_s16le_16
cloud_storage_url: "https://storage.googleapis.com/my-bucket/folder/audio.mp3"
source_url: "https://storage.googleapis.com/my-bucket/folder/audio.mp3"
webhook: false
webhook_id: string
temperature: 0
seed: 12345
use_multi_channel: false
multichannel_output_style: separate
webhook_metadata: "{\"user_id\": \"123\", \"session_id\": \"abc-def-ghi\"}"
entity_detection: string
no_verbatim: false
use_speaker_library: false
detect_speaker_roles: false
entity_redaction: string
entity_redaction_mode: enumerated_entity_type
keyterms: []
```

<h3 id="speech-to-text-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|query|string \| null|false|A single-use authentication token created via POST /v1/single-use-token/batch_scribe. This token can only be used once and expires after 15 minutes. Alternative to API key or bearer token authentication for frontend clients.|
|enable_logging|query|boolean|false|When enable_logging is set to false zero retention mode will be used for the request. This will mean log and transcript storage features are unavailable for this request. Zero retention mode may only be used by enterprise customers.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Speech_to_Text_v1_speech_to_text_post](#schemabody_speech_to_text_v1_speech_to_text_post)|true|none|
|» model_id|body|string|true|The ID of the model to use for transcription.|
|» file|body|string(binary) \| null|false|The file to transcribe (100ms minimum audio length). All major audio and video formats are supported. Exactly one of the file or cloud_storage_url parameters must be provided. The file size must be less than 5.0GB.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» language_code|body|string \| null|false|An ISO-639-1 or ISO-639-3 language_code corresponding to the language of the audio file. Can sometimes improve transcription performance if known beforehand. Defaults to null, in this case the language is predicted automatically.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» transcript_edit|body|string \| null|false|Natural-language instruction applied to the final transcript (max 2000 characters). The edited text is returned in 'edited_transcript' alongside the original transcript. Cannot be combined with entity_detection, entity_redaction or use_multi_channel. Usage of this parameter will incur an additional 30% surcharge on the base transcription cost, billed for at least 10 seconds of audio.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» tag_audio_events|body|boolean|false|Whether to tag audio events like (laughter), (footsteps), etc. in the transcription.|
|» num_speakers|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum amount of speakers talking in the uploaded file. Can help with predicting who speaks when. The maximum amount of speakers that can be predicted is 32. Defaults to null, in this case the amount of speakers is set to the maximum value the model supports.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» timestamps_granularity|body|string|false|The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription. 'word' provides word-level timestamps and 'character' provides character-level timestamps per word.|
|» diarize|body|boolean|false|Whether to annotate which speaker is currently talking in the uploaded file.|
|» diarization_threshold|body|number \| null|false|Diarization threshold to apply during speaker diarization. A higher value means there will be a lower chance of one speaker being diarized as two different speakers but also a higher chance of two different speakers being diarized as one speaker (less total speakers predicted). A low value means there will be a higher chance of one speaker being diarized as two different speakers but also a lower chance of two different speakers being diarized as one speaker (more total speakers predicted). Can only be set when diarize=True and num_speakers=None. Defaults to None, in which case we will choose a threshold based on the model_id (0.22 usually).|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» additional_formats|body|[AdditionalFormats](#schemaadditionalformats)|false|A list of additional formats to export the transcript to.|
|» file_format|body|string|false|The format of input audio. Options are 'pcm_s16le_16' or 'other' For `pcm_s16le_16`, the input audio must be 16-bit PCM at a 16kHz sample rate, single channel (mono), and little-endian byte order. Latency will be lower than with passing an encoded waveform.|
|» cloud_storage_url|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** [Deprecated] This parameter is deprecated and will be removed in the future. Use 'source_url' instead.The HTTPS URL of the file to transcribe. Exactly one of the file or cloud_storage_url parameters must be provided. The file must be accessible via HTTPS and the file size must be less than 2GB. Any valid HTTPS URL is accepted, including URLs from cloud storage providers (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Cloudflare R2, etc.), CDNs, or any other HTTPS source. URLs can be pre-signed or include authentication tokens in query parameters.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» source_url|body|string \| null|false|The URL of an audio or video file to transcribe. Supports hosted video or audio files, YouTube video URLs, TikTok video URLs, and other video hosting services.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» webhook|body|boolean|false|Whether to send the transcription result to configured speech-to-text webhooks.  If set the request will return early without the transcription, which will be delivered later via webhook.|
|» webhook_id|body|string \| null|false|Optional specific webhook ID to send the transcription result to. Only valid when webhook is set to true. If not provided, transcription will be sent to all configured speech-to-text webhooks.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» temperature|body|number \| null|false|Controls the randomness of the transcription output. Accepts values between 0.0 and 2.0, where higher values result in more diverse and less deterministic results. If omitted, we will use a temperature based on the model you selected which is usually 0.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» seed|body|integer \| null|false|If specified, our system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should return the same result. Determinism is not guaranteed. Must be an integer between 0 and 2147483647.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» use_multi_channel|body|boolean|false|Whether the audio file contains multiple channels where each channel contains a single speaker. When enabled, each channel is transcribed independently. By default a separate transcript is returned per channel; set multichannel_output_style='combined' to instead receive a single transcript with all channels merged and sorted by time. Each word in the response includes a 'channel_index' field indicating which channel it was spoken on. A maximum of 5 channels is supported. Each channel is billed independently at the full audio duration, so cost scales linearly with the number of channels.|
|» multichannel_output_style|body|string|false|Controls the response shape when use_multi_channel is enabled. 'separate' (default) returns one transcript per channel under 'transcripts'. 'combined' merges all channels into a single transcript whose words are sorted by start time, each carrying a 'channel_index' - matching the single-channel response shape. 'combined' requires timestamps (timestamps_granularity must not be 'none') and does not support entity detection or redaction.|
|» webhook_metadata|body|string \| object \| null|false|Optional metadata to be included in the webhook response. This should be a JSON string representing an object with a maximum depth of 2 levels and maximum size of 16KB. Useful for tracking internal IDs, job references, or other contextual information.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» entity_detection|body|string \| [string] \| null|false|Detect entities in the transcript. Can be 'all' to detect all entities, a single entity type or category string, or a list of entity types/categories. Categories include 'pii', 'phi', 'pci', 'other', 'offensive_language'. When enabled, detected entities will be returned in the 'entities' field with their text, type, and character positions.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» no_verbatim|body|boolean|false|If true, the transcription will not have any filler words, false starts and non-speech sounds.|
|» use_speaker_library|body|boolean|false|Whether to use the speaker library for identifying known speakers during diarization. When enabled and diarize is true, detected speakers will be matched against registered speakers in the workspace's speaker library.|
|» detect_speaker_roles|body|boolean|false|Whether to detect speaker roles (agent vs customer). Requires diarize=true. Cannot be used with use_multi_channel=true. When enabled, speaker_id values will be 'agent' and 'customer' instead of 'speaker_0', 'speaker_1', etc. Usage incurs an additional 10% surcharge on base transcription cost.|
|» entity_redaction|body|string \| [string] \| null|false|Redact entities from the transcript text. Accepts the same format as entity_detection: 'all', a category ('pii', 'phi'), or specific entity types. Must be a subset of entity_detection. When redaction is enabled, the entities field will not be returned.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» entity_redaction_mode|body|string|false|How to format redacted entities. 'redacted' replaces with {REDACTED}, 'entity_type' replaces with {ENTITY_TYPE}, 'enumerated_entity_type' replaces with {ENTITY_TYPE_N} where N enumerates each occurrence. Only used when entity_redaction is set.|
|» keyterms|body|[string]|false|A list of keyterms to bias the transcription towards.           The keyterms are words or phrases you want the model to recognise more accurately.           The number of keyterms cannot exceed 1000.           The length of each keyterm must be less than 50 characters.           Keyterms can contain at most 5 words (after normalisation).           For example ["hello", "world", "technical term"].           The following characters are not supported: `<`, `>`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `\`.           Usage of this parameter will incur an additional 20% surcharge on the base transcription cost.           When more than 100 keyterms are provided, a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds applies per request.|

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-forced-alignment">forced-alignment</h1>

Force align an audio file to a text transcript to get precise word-level and character level timing information. Response is a list of characters with their start and end times as milliseconds elapsed from the start of the recording.

## Create Forced Alignment

<a id="opIdforced_alignment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/forced-alignment \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'text=string'
```

`POST /v1/forced-alignment`

Force align an audio file to text. Use this endpoint to get the timing information for each character and word in an audio file based on a provided text transcript.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
text: string
```

<h3 id="create-forced-alignment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Create_forced_alignment_v1_forced_alignment_post](#schemabody_create_forced_alignment_v1_forced_alignment_post)|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The file to align. All major audio formats are supported. The file size must be less than 1GB.|
|» text|body|string|true|The text to align with the audio. The input text can be in any format, however diarization is not supported at this time.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "characters": [
    {
      "end": 0.02,
      "start": 0,
      "text": "H"
    }
  ],
  "words": [
    {
      "end": 1.02,
      "loss": 0.12,
      "start": 0,
      "text": "Hello"
    }
  ],
  "loss": 0
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-forced-alignment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[ForcedAlignmentResponseModel](#schemaforcedalignmentresponsemodel)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Register Media

<a id="opIdpublic_register_media"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/productions/orders/string/media \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'declared_language=string' \
  -F 'media=string' \

  -F 'media_url_filename=string' \
  -F 'media_url_content_type=string'
```

`POST /v1/productions/orders/{order_id}/media`

Registers a media file with an order, either by uploading it directly or by providing a URL to fetch it from. Exactly one of `media` or `media_url` must be provided. The registered media can then be referenced when adding order items.

> Body parameter

```yaml
declared_language: string
media: string
media_url: string
media_url_filename: string
media_url_content_type: string
```

<h3 id="register-media-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|order_id|path|[OrderId](#schemaorderid)|true|The ID of the order to which this media will be attached.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Register_media_v1_productions_orders__order_id__media_post](#schemabody_register_media_v1_productions_orders__order_id__media_post)|true|none|
|» declared_language|body|string|true|The language code of the media content (e.g. 'en', 'es-ES'). Must be a supported source language for some order item kind.|
|» media|body|string(binary) \| null|false|The media file to upload. Mutually exclusive with media_url.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» media_url|body|string \| null|false|A URL to fetch the media file from. Mutually exclusive with media.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» media_url_filename|body|string \| null|false|The filename for URL-sourced media (e.g. 'example.mp4'). Required when using media_url.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» media_url_content_type|body|string \| null|false|The MIME type for URL-sourced media (e.g. 'video/mp4'). Required when using media_url.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

{
  "media_id": "prodmedia_01jgb2zd68f8f9tfvbb968wb8z"
}
```

    }

## Submit Order

<a id="opIdpublic_submit_order"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/productions/orders/string/submit \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /v1/productions/orders/{order_id}/submit`

Submits an open order for processing. The order must have at least one item. Once submitted, items can no longer be modified.

Upon submission, the workspace will be charged for the order. The quote is based on information extracted from the uploaded media, such as its duration. The quote may not be available immediately; if you wish to see the quote before submission, you may need to poll the order details until the quote is ready.

<h3 id="submit-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|order_id|path|[OrderId](#schemaorderid)|true|The ID of the order.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

{
  "order_id": "prodorder_01jgatk6h0fwxrtbjade61yqhx",
  "state": "submitted",

}

{
  "detail": [

## Edit Voice Settings

<a id="opIdedit_voice_settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM/settings/edit \
  -X POST \

`POST /v1/voices/{voice_id}/settings/edit`

Edit your settings for a specific voice. "similarity_boost" corresponds to "Clarity + Similarity Enhancement" in the web app and "stability" corresponds to "Stability" slider in the web app.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "similarity_boost": 1,
  "speed": 1,
  "stability": 1,
  "style": 0,
  "use_speaker_boost": true
}
```

<h3 id="edit-voice-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice_id|path|string|true|Voice ID to be used, you can use https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices to list all the available voices.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[VoiceSettingsResponseModel](#schemavoicesettingsresponsemodel)|true|none|
|» stability|body|number \| null|false|Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values introduce broader emotional range for the voice. Higher values can result in a monotonous voice with limited emotion.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» use_speaker_boost|body|boolean \| null|false|This setting boosts the similarity to the original speaker. Using this setting requires a slightly higher computational load, which in turn increases latency.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» similarity_boost|body|number \| null|false|Determines how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice when attempting to replicate it.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» style|body|number \| null|false|Determines the style exaggeration of the voice. This setting attempts to amplify the style of the original speaker. It does consume additional computational resources and might increase latency if set to anything other than 0.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» speed|body|number \| null|false|Adjusts the speed of the voice. A value of 1.0 is the default speed, while values less than 1.0 slow down the speech, and values greater than 1.0 speed it up.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» clone_strength|body|number \| null|false|Controls how closely the voice matches the professional voice clone samples, from 0 (low) to 1 (high). We recommend 0 for most use cases. Increase this value only if you experience issues with the default settings. Only applies to professional voice clones fine-tuned for the selected v4 model.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

`POST /v1/voices/{voice_id}/edit`

name: John Smith
files:
  - string
remove_background_noise: true
description: An old American male voice with a slight hoarseness in his throat. Perfect for news.

moderate_metadata: false

|» files|body|[string(binary)]|false|Audio files to add to the voice|
|» remove_background_noise|body|boolean|false|If set will remove background noise for voice samples using our audio isolation model. If the samples do not include background noise, it can make the quality worse.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|A description of the voice.|

## Get Voices V2

<a id="opIdget_user_voices_v2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v2/voices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/voices`

Gets a list of all available voices for a user with search, filtering and pagination.

<h3 id="get-voices-v2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|next_page_token|query|string \| null|false|The next page token to use for pagination. Returned from the previous request. Use this in combination with the has_more flag for reliable pagination.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|How many voices to return at maximum. Can not exceed 100, defaults to 10. Page 0 may include more voices due to default voices being included.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Search term to filter voices by. Searches in name, description, labels, category.|
|sort|query|string \| null|false|Which field to sort by, one of 'created_at_unix' or 'name'. 'created_at_unix' may not be available for older voices.|
|sort_direction|query|string \| null|false|Which direction to sort the voices in. 'asc' or 'desc'.|
|voice_type|query|string \| null|false|Type of the voice to filter by. One of 'personal', 'community', 'default', 'workspace', 'non-default', 'non-community', 'saved'. 'non-default' is equal to all but 'default'. 'non-community' is equal to 'personal' and 'workspace' combined (excludes library copies). 'saved' is equal to non-default, but includes default voices if they have been added to a collection.|
|category|query|string \| null|false|Category of the voice to filter by. One of 'premade', 'cloned', 'generated', 'professional'|
|fine_tuning_state|query|string \| null|false|State of the voice's fine tuning to filter by. Applicable only to professional voices clones. One of 'draft', 'not_verified', 'not_started', 'queued', 'fine_tuning', 'fine_tuned', 'failed', 'delayed'|
|collection_id|query|string \| null|false|Collection ID to filter voices by.|
|gender|query|string \| null|false|Gender used for filtering, based on the voice's 'gender' label.|
|age|query|string \| null|false|Age used for filtering, based on the voice's 'age' label.|
|language|query|[string] \| null|false|Languages used for filtering, based on the voice's 'language' label. Voices matching any of the given languages are returned.|
|accent|query|string \| null|false|Accent used for filtering, based on the voice's 'accent' label.|
|use_cases|query|[string] \| null|false|Use cases used for filtering, based on the voice's 'use_case' label. Voices matching any of the given use cases are returned.|
|min_notice_period_days|query|integer \| null|false|Filter to voices whose sharing notice period is at least the given number of days.|
|include_custom_rates|query|boolean \| null|false|Whether to include voices that have a custom sharing rate. Defaults to including them.|
|include_live_moderated|query|boolean \| null|false|Whether to include voices that have live moderation enabled. Defaults to including them.|
|high_quality|query|boolean \| null|false|When true, only return studio-quality voices (those whose category is 'high_quality').|
|include_total_count|query|boolean|false|Whether to include the total count of voices found in the response. NOTE: The total_count value is a live snapshot and may change between requests as users create, modify, or delete voices. For pagination, rely on the has_more flag instead. Only enable this when you actually need the total count (e.g., for display purposes), as it incurs a performance cost.|
|voice_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Voice IDs to lookup by. Maximum 100 voice IDs.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "voices": [
    {
      "available_for_tiers": [
        "creator",
        "enterprise"
      ],
      "category": "professional",
      "description": "A warm, expressive voice with a touch of humor.",
      "fine_tuning": {
        "is_allowed_to_fine_tune": true,
        "manual_verification_requested": false,
        "state": {
          "eleven_multilingual_v2": "fine_tuned"
        },
        "verification_attempts_count": 2,

      },

        "eleven_multilingual_v2",
        "eleven_v2_5_flash",
        "eleven_flash_v2_5",
        "eleven_turbo_v2"
      ],
      "is_legacy": false,

      "labels": {
        "accent": "American",

## Replicate Voice To Isolated Environment

<a id="opIdreplicate_voice_to_isolated_environment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM/replicate-to-isolated-environment \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "target_workspace_id": "string",
    "preserve_voice_id": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/voices/{voice_id}/replicate-to-isolated-environment`

Replicates an Instant Voice Clone or Voice Design voice to a workspace in a different data residency. The target workspace must belong to the same consolidated billing group. The user must have VOICES_WRITE in the source workspace, and be an admin on the source voice. Human users (i.e. not service accounts) must also have VOICES_WRITE in the target workspace. This endpoint is available on the central environment only.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "target_workspace_id": "string",
  "preserve_voice_id": true
}
```

<h3 id="replicate-voice-to-isolated-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice_id|path|string|true|Voice ID to be used, you can use https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices to list all the available voices.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[ReplicateVoiceToIsolatedEnvironmentRequestModel](#schemareplicatevoicetoisolatedenvironmentrequestmodel)|true|none|
|» target_workspace_id|body|string|true|ID of the workspace to replicate the voice into. It must belong to the same consolidated billing group as the calling workspace; the target's data residency is derived from that link.|
|» preserve_voice_id|body|boolean|false|When true (default) the replicated voice keeps the same voice ID in the target residency; set to false to assign a new voice ID.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "voice_id": "21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="replicate-voice-to-isolated-environment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[ReplicateVoiceToIsolatedEnvironmentResponseModel](#schemareplicatevoicetoisolatedenvironmentresponsemodel)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

`POST /v1/voices/add`

files:
  - string
remove_background_noise: true

|» labels|body|object \| string \| null|false|Labels for the voice. Keys can be language, accent, gender, or age.|

## Get Similar Library Voices

<a id="opIdget_similar_library_voices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/similar-voices \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'audio_file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'similarity_threshold=0.5' \
  -F 'top_k=10'
```

`POST /v1/similar-voices`

Returns a list of shared voices similar to the provided audio sample. If neither similarity_threshold nor top_k is provided, we will apply default values.

> Body parameter

```yaml
audio_file: string
similarity_threshold: 0.5
top_k: 10
```

<h3 id="get-similar-library-voices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Get_similar_library_voices_v1_similar_voices_post](#schemabody_get_similar_library_voices_v1_similar_voices_post)|false|none|
|» audio_file|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» similarity_threshold|body|number \| null|false|Threshold for voice similarity between provided sample and library voices. Values range from 0 to 2. The smaller the value the more similar voices will be returned.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» top_k|body|integer \| null|false|Number of most similar voices to return. If similarity_threshold is provided, less than this number of voices may be returned. Values range from 1 to 100.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-speech-history">speech-history</h1>

Accesses your speech history. Your speech history is a list of all your created audio including its metadata using our text-to-speech and speech-to-speech models.

## List Generated Items

<a id="opIdget_speech_history"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/history`

Returns a list of your generated audio (e.g. text to speech, speech to speech, Studio, dubbing). Music and SFX generations are not included and cannot currently be retrieved via the API.

<h3 id="list-generated-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|date_before_unix|query|integer \| null|false|Unix timestamp to filter history items before this date (exclusive).|

`POST /v1/history/download`

Download one or more history items. If one history item ID is provided, we will return a single audio file. If more than one history item IDs are provided, we will provide the history items packed into a .zip file.

    "string"
  ],
  "output_format": "string"

## Set Workspace Third-Party Disabling Policy

<a id="opIdset_third_party_disabling_policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/workspaces/api-keys/third-party-disabling \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "third_party_disable_allowed": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/workspaces/api-keys/third-party-disabling`

Set the workspace-wide Third-Party Disabling policy. When set, it forces, for every API key in the workspace, whether the holder of a key (potentially a third party who found it) may disable it via the self-disable endpoint or when it leaks publicly — overriding each key's own setting. Pass `true` to allow it for all keys, `false` to forbid it for all keys, or `null` to clear the override so per-key values and the plan default apply again. Workspace admins only.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "third_party_disable_allowed": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-workspace-third-party-disabling-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Set_workspace_Third_Party_Disabling_policy_v1_workspaces_api_keys_third_party_disabling_post](#schemabody_set_workspace_third_party_disabling_policy_v1_workspaces_api_keys_third_party_disabling_post)|false|none|
|» third_party_disable_allowed|body|boolean \| null|false|`true` forces every key in the workspace to be disable-able by its holder; `false` forbids it for every key; `null` clears the override (per-key values and the plan default apply).|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Invite User

<a id="opIdinvite_user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/workspace/invites/add \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "john.doe@testmail.com",
    "workspace_permission": "workspace_member",
    "seat_type": "workspace_member",
    "group_ids": [
      "group_id_1",
      "group_id_2"
    ],
    "usage_limit": 5000
  }'
```

`POST /v1/workspace/invites/add`

Sends an email invitation to join your workspace to the provided email. If the user doesn't have an account they will be prompted to create one. If the user accepts this invite they will be added as a user to your workspace and your subscription using one of your seats. This endpoint may only be called by workspace members with the WORKSPACE_MEMBERS_INVITE permission. If the user is already in the workspace a 400 error will be returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "john.doe@testmail.com",
  "workspace_permission": "workspace_member",
  "seat_type": "workspace_member",
  "group_ids": [
    "group_id_1",
    "group_id_2"
  ],
  "usage_limit": 5000
}
```

<h3 id="invite-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Invite_user_v1_workspace_invites_add_post](#schemabody_invite_user_v1_workspace_invites_add_post)|true|none|
|» email|body|string|true|The email of the customer|
|» workspace_permission|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The workspace permission of the user. This is deprecated, use `seat_type` instead.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» seat_type|body|[SeatType](#schemaseattype) \| null|false|The seat type of the user|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[SeatType](#schemaseattype)|false|Seat types for workspace members.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» group_ids|body|[string] \| null|false|The group ids of the user|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» usage_limit|body|integer \| null|false|Monthly credit usage limit for the invitee. Omit or set to null for no custom cap.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## Share Workspace Resource

<a id="opIdshare_resource_endpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/workspace/resources/string/share \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "role": "admin",
    "resource_type": "voice",
    "user_email": "string",
    "group_id": "string",
    "workspace_api_key_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/workspace/resources/{resource_id}/share`

Grants a role (one of 'admin', 'editor', 'commenter', or 'viewer') on a workspace resource to a user, group, or workspace (service account) API key. This overrides any existing role the target has on the resource. To target a user or service account, pass only the user email; the user must be in your workspace. To target a group, pass only the group id. To target a workspace (service account) API key, pass the api key id; the resource will be shared with the service account associated with that key. You must have admin access to the resource to share it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "role": "admin",
  "resource_type": "voice",
  "user_email": "string",
  "group_id": "string",
  "workspace_api_key_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="share-workspace-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|resource_id|path|string|true|The ID of the target resource.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Share_workspace_resource_v1_workspace_resources__resource_id__share_post](#schemabody_share_workspace_resource_v1_workspace_resources__resource_id__share_post)|true|none|
|» role|body|string|true|Role to grant to the target: one of 'admin', 'editor', 'commenter', or 'viewer'.|
|» resource_type|body|[WorkspaceResourceType](#schemaworkspaceresourcetype)|true|Resource type of the target resource.|
|» user_email|body|string \| null|false|The email of the user or service account.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» group_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the target group. Use 'default' to set the resource's baseline role — every workspace member receives this role unless they hold a higher one through a direct user grant, group membership, or workspace (service account) API key.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» workspace_api_key_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the target workspace (service account) API key. This is not the API key string itself that you pass in the header for authentication — it is the key's ID, which workspace admins can find under Developers → Service Accounts.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

`POST /v1/text-to-voice/create-previews`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated.** Use `POST /v1/text-to-voice/design` instead. Generate a custom voice based on voice description. This method returns a list of voice previews. Each preview has a generated_voice_id and a sample of the voice as base64 encoded mp3 audio. To create the voice use `POST /v1/text-to-voice` with the chosen `generated_voice_id`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "voice_description": "A sassy squeaky mouse",
  "text": "Every act of kindness, no matter how small, carries value and can make a difference, as no gesture of goodwill is ever wasted.",
  "auto_generate_text": false,
  "loudness": 0.5,
  "quality": 0.9,
  "seed": 11,
  "guidance_scale": 5,
  "should_enhance": true
}
```

<h3 id="deprecated-generate-a-voice-preview-from-description-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|output_format|query|[AllowedOutputFormats](#schemaallowedoutputformats)|false|Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[VoicePreviewsRequestModel](#schemavoicepreviewsrequestmodel)|true|none|
|» voice_description|body|string|true|Description to use for the created voice.|
|» text|body|string \| null|false|Text to generate, text length has to be between 100 and 1000.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» auto_generate_text|body|boolean|false|Whether to automatically generate a text suitable for the voice description.|
|» loudness|body|number|false|Controls the volume level of the generated voice. -1 is quietest, 1 is loudest, 0 corresponds to roughly -24 LUFS.|
|» quality|body|number|false|Higher quality results in better voice output but less variety.|
|» seed|body|integer \| null|false|Random number that controls the voice generation. Same seed with same inputs produces same voice.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» guidance_scale|body|number|false|Controls how closely the AI follows the prompt. Lower numbers give the AI more freedom to be creative, while higher numbers force it to stick more to the prompt. High numbers can cause voice to sound artificial or robotic. We recommend to use longer, more detailed prompts at lower Guidance Scale.|
|» should_enhance|body|boolean|false|Whether to enhance the voice description using AI to add more detail and improve voice generation quality. When enabled, the system will automatically expand simple prompts into more detailed voice descriptions. Defaults to False|

## Remix A Voice.

<a id="opIdtext_to_voice_remix"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-voice/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM/remix \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "voice_description": "Make the voice have a higher pitch.",
    "text": "Every act of kindness, no matter how small, carries value and can make a difference, as no gesture of goodwill is ever wasted.",
    "auto_generate_text": false,
    "loudness": 0.5,
    "seed": 11,
    "guidance_scale": 5,
    "stream_previews": true,
    "remixing_session_id": "123",
    "remixing_session_iteration_id": "123",
    "prompt_strength": 0.25
  }'
```

`POST /v1/text-to-voice/{voice_id}/remix`

Remix an existing voice via a prompt. This method returns a list of voice previews. Each preview has a generated_voice_id and a sample of the voice as base64 encoded mp3 audio. To create a voice use the generated_voice_id of the preferred preview with the /v1/text-to-voice endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "voice_description": "Make the voice have a higher pitch.",
  "text": "Every act of kindness, no matter how small, carries value and can make a difference, as no gesture of goodwill is ever wasted.",
  "auto_generate_text": false,
  "loudness": 0.5,
  "seed": 11,
  "guidance_scale": 5,
  "stream_previews": true,
  "remixing_session_id": "123",
  "remixing_session_iteration_id": "123",
  "prompt_strength": 0.25
}
```

<h3 id="remix-a-voice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice_id|path|string|true|Voice ID to be used, you can use https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices to list all the available voices.|
|output_format|query|[AllowedOutputFormats](#schemaallowedoutputformats)|false|Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[VoiceRemixRequestModel](#schemavoiceremixrequestmodel)|true|none|

|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» auto_generate_text|body|boolean|false|Whether to automatically generate a text suitable for the voice description.|
|» loudness|body|number|false|Controls the volume level of the generated voice. -1 is quietest, 1 is loudest, 0 corresponds to roughly -24 LUFS.|
|» seed|body|integer \| null|false|Random number that controls the voice generation. Same seed with same inputs produces same voice.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|

High numbers can cause voice to sound artificial or robotic. We recommend to use longer, more detailed prompts at lower Guidance Scale.|

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-text-to-dialogue">text-to-dialogue</h1>

Generate multi-speaker dialogue from a script using different voices.

## Text To Dialogue (Multi-Voice)

<a id="opIdtext_to_dialogue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-dialogue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "inputs": [
      {
        "text": "Hello, how are you?",
        "voice_id": "bYTqZQo3Jz7LQtmGTgwi"
      },
      {
        "text": "I'\''m doing well, thank you!",
        "voice_id": "6lCwbsX1yVjD49QmpkTR"
      }
    ],
    "model_id": "eleven_v3",
    "language_code": "en",
    "settings": {
      "stability": 0.5
    },
    "previous_text": "string",
    "future_text": "string",
    "pronunciation_dictionary_locators": [
      {
        "pronunciation_dictionary_id": "test",
        "version_id": "id2"
      }
    ],
    "seed": 12345,
    "apply_text_normalization": true,
    "use_pvc_as_ivc": true,
    "previous_request_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "next_request_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "audio_effects": {
      "filter_preset_id": "string",
      "distance": 0,
      "environment_id": "string",
      "background_noise_id": "string",
      "send_level": 1,
      "pan": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/text-to-dialogue`

Converts a list of text and voice ID pairs into speech (dialogue) and returns audio.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "text": "Hello, how are you?",
      "voice_id": "bYTqZQo3Jz7LQtmGTgwi"
    },
    {
      "text": "I'm doing well, thank you!",
      "voice_id": "6lCwbsX1yVjD49QmpkTR"
    }
  ],
  "model_id": "eleven_v3",
  "language_code": "en",
  "settings": {
    "stability": 0.5
  },
  "previous_text": "string",
  "future_text": "string",
  "pronunciation_dictionary_locators": [
    {
      "pronunciation_dictionary_id": "test",
      "version_id": "id2"
    }
  ],
  "seed": 12345,
  "apply_text_normalization": true,
  "use_pvc_as_ivc": true,
  "previous_request_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "next_request_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "audio_effects": {
    "filter_preset_id": "string",
    "distance": 0,
    "environment_id": "string",
    "background_noise_id": "string",
    "send_level": 1,
    "pan": 0
  }
}
```

PCM and WAV formats with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.|

When set to 'auto', the system will automatically decide whether to apply text normalization (e.g., spelling out numbers). curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-dialogue/stream/with-timestamps \

      {

      }

      "stability": 0.5

      "string"

      "send_level": 1,
      "pan": 0
    }
  }'

`POST /v1/text-to-dialogue/stream/with-timestamps`

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-sound-generation">sound-generation</h1>

## Sound Generation

<a id="opIdsound_generation"></a>

> Code samples

    "prompt_influence": 0.3,
    "model_id": "eleven_text_to_sound_v2"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/sound-generation`

Turn text into sound effects for your videos, voice-overs or video games using the most advanced sound effects models in the world.

  "text": "A large, ancient wooden door slowly opening in an eerie, abandoned castle..",
  "loop": false,

Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM and WAV formats with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.|

To specify multiple dictionaries use multiple --form lines in your curl, such as --form 'pronunciation_dictionary_locators="{\"pronunciation_dictionary_id\":\"Vmd4Zor6fplcA7WrINey\",\"version_id\":\"hRPaxjlTdR7wFMhV4w0b\"}"' --form 'pronunciation_dictionary_locators="{\"pronunciation_dictionary_id\":\"JzWtcGQMJ6bnlWwyMo7e\",\"version_id\":\"lbmwxiLu4q6txYxgdZqn\"}"'.|

## Generate Composition Plan

<a id="opIdcompose_plan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/music/plan \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "string",
    "music_length_ms": 3000,
    "source_composition_plan": {
      "negative_global_styles": [
        "metal",
        "hip-hop",
        "country"
      ],
      "positive_global_styles": [
        "pop",
        "rock",
        "jazz"
      ],
      "sections": [
        {
          "duration_ms": 10000,
          "lines": [
            "Verse 1 lyrics"
          ],
          "negative_local_styles": [
            "metal",
            "hip-hop",
            "country"
          ],
          "positive_local_styles": [
            "pop",
            "rock",
            "jazz"
          ],
          "section_name": "Verse 1"
        }
      ]
    },
    "model_id": "music_v1"
  }'
```

|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

Providing the same seed with the same parameters can help achieve more consistent results, but exact reproducibility is not guaranteed and outputs may change across system updates. Cannot be used in conjunction with prompt.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» force_instrumental|body|boolean|false|If true, guarantees that the generated song will be instrumental. If false, the song may or may not be instrumental depending on the `prompt`. Can only be used with `prompt`.|
|» finetune_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the finetune to use for the generation|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» finetune_strength|body|number|false|How strongly the finetune influences the generation. Defaults to 1.0 (full strength). Lower values soften the influence of the finetune, leaving more room for prompt-level steering. Only meaningful when `finetune_id` is also provided.|
|» use_phonetic_names|body|boolean|false|If true, proper names in the prompt will be phonetically spelled in the lyrics for better pronunciation by the music model. The original names will be restored in word timestamps.|

Only used with `composition_plan` and only applies to `music_v1`; for `music_v2` and `music_v2_5` section durations are always enforced and this is ignored. When false for `music_v1`, the model may adjust individual section durations for better quality and latency, while preserving the total song duration from the plan.|

|» sign_with_c2pa|body|boolean|false|Whether to sign the generated song with C2PA. Applicable only for mp3 files.|

      "pop",
      "rock",
      "jazz"
    ],
    "sections": [
      {
        "duration_ms": 10000,
        "lines": [
          "Verse 1 lyrics"
        ],
        "negative_local_styles": [
          "metal",
          "hip-hop",
          "country"
        ],
        "positive_local_styles": [
          "pop",
          "rock",
          "jazz"
        ],
        "section_name": "Verse 1"
      }
    ]
  },
  "music_length_ms": 3000,
  "model_id": "music_v1",
  "seed": 0,
  "force_instrumental": false,
  "finetune_id": "string",
  "finetune_strength": 1,
  "use_phonetic_names": false,
  "store_for_inpainting": false
}
```

## Upload Music

<a id="opIdupload_song"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/music/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'extract_composition_plan=false' \
  -F 'with_timestamps=false' \
  -F 'with_waveform_visual=false'
```

`POST /v1/music/upload`

Upload a music file to be later used for inpainting. Price for uploading is the same as the one for song generation. All uploaded content gets inspected for copyright infringement. If copyrighted content is detected, half of the request cost is still charged.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
extract_composition_plan: false
with_timestamps: false
with_waveform_visual: false
```

<h3 id="upload-music-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Upload_music_v1_music_upload_post](#schemabody_upload_music_v1_music_upload_post)|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The audio file to upload.|
|» extract_composition_plan|body|boolean \| [MusicModelID](#schemamusicmodelid)|false|Whether to generate and return the composition plan for the uploaded song. Pass a model id (`music_v1`, `music_v2` or `music_v2_5`) to control which composition plan format is returned. Passing `true`/`false` is deprecated; `true` defaults to the `music_v1` plan format. Enabling this will increase the latency.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[MusicModelID](#schemamusicmodelid)|false|none|
|» with_timestamps|body|boolean|false|Whether to transcribe the uploaded song and return word-level timestamps. If True, the response will include words_timestamps but will increase the latency.|
|» with_waveform_visual|body|boolean|false|Whether to return the visual waveform of the uploaded song.|

## Stem Separation

<a id="opIdseparate_song_stems"></a>

curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/music/stem-separation \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'stem_variation_id=six_stems_v1' \
  -F 'sign_with_c2pa=false'
```

`POST /v1/music/stem-separation`

Separate an audio file into individual stems. This endpoint might have high latency, depending on the length of the audio file.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
stem_variation_id: six_stems_v1
sign_with_c2pa: false
```

<h3 id="stem-separation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|output_format|query|[AllowedOutputFormats](#schemaallowedoutputformats)|false|Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.|
|enable_logging|query|boolean|false|When enable_logging is set to false zero retention mode will be used for the request. Zero retention mode may only be used by enterprise customers.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The audio file to separate into stems.|
|» stem_variation_id|body|string|false|The id of the stem variation to use.|
|» sign_with_c2pa|body|boolean|false|Whether to sign the generated song with C2PA. Applicable only for mp3 files.|

<a id="opIdget_finetunes"></a>
