`GET /v1/music/finetunes`

List music finetunes accessible to you (your own, workspace-shared, and ElevenLabs-curated), with optional filtering, sorting, and cursor pagination.

<h3 id="get-music-finetunes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching the next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|How many finetunes to return. Max 150, default 50.|
|visibility|query|[FinetuneVisibility](#schemafinetunevisibility) \| null|false|Filter by visibility. 'private' returns private finetunes; 'workspace' returns workspace-shared finetunes; 'public' returns public finetunes, which are currently ElevenLabs curated finetunes. Omit to return all accessible finetunes.|
|created_by|query|[FinetuneCreatedBy](#schemafinetunecreatedby) \| null|false|Filter by creator. 'self' returns finetunes you created; 'workspace' returns finetunes created by workspace teammates; 'elevenlabs' returns ElevenLabs curated finetunes. Omit to return finetunes from all creators.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort by field (created_at or name)|
|sort_direction|query|string|false|Sort direction (asc or desc)|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-video-to-music">video-to-music</h1>

Generate music that matches the content and mood of a video.

## Video To Music

<a id="opIdvideo_to_music"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/music/video-to-music \
  -X POST \
  -F 'videos=["string"]' \
  -F 'description=string' \
  -F 'tags=[]' \
  -F 'model_id=music_v1' \
  -F 'add_sfx=false' \
  -F 'separate_tracks=false' \
  -F 'use_audio_as_reference=false' \
  -F 'sign_with_c2pa=false'
```

`POST /v1/music/video-to-music`

Generate background music from one or more video files. Videos are combined in order. Optional description and style tags influence the generated music.

> Body parameter

```yaml
videos:
  - string
description: string
tags: []
model_id: music_v1
add_sfx: false
separate_tracks: false
use_audio_as_reference: false
sign_with_c2pa: false
```

<h3 id="video-to-music-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|output_format|query|[AllowedOutputFormats](#schemaallowedoutputformats)|false|Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.|
|enable_logging|query|boolean|false|When enable_logging is set to false zero retention mode will be used for the request. Zero retention mode may only be used by enterprise customers.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Video_to_Music_v1_music_video_to_music_post](#schemabody_video_to_music_v1_music_video_to_music_post)|true|none|
|» videos|body|[string(binary)]|true|<br>            One or more video files sent via FormData array (multipart/form-data). They will be combined into one codec in order.<br>            A maximum of 10 videos is allowed, where the total size of the combined video is limited to 200MB.<br>            In total, the video can be up to 600 seconds long. Note that combining multiple videos may increase the request duration significantly. If possible, combine the videos beforehand.<br>            |
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Optional text description of the music you want. A maximum of 4100 characters is allowed.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Optional list of style tags (e.g. ['upbeat', 'cinematic']). A maximum of 10 tags is allowed.|
|» model_id|body|[MusicModelID](#schemamusicmodelid)|false|The model to use for the generation.|
|» add_sfx|body|boolean|false|When true, incorporate SFX cues from the video.|
|» separate_tracks|body|boolean|false|When true, return a ZIP with separate music and SFX audio tracks instead of a single mixed file. Use this for more flexibility to layer the tracks.|
|» use_audio_as_reference|body|boolean|false|When true, analyze the video's audio track and use its genres, BPM, instrumentation, mood, and arc as reference characteristics for music generation.|
|» sign_with_c2pa|body|boolean|false|Whether to sign the generated song with C2PA. Applicable only for mp3 files.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|output_format|mp3_22050_32|
|output_format|mp3_24000_48|
|output_format|mp3_44100_32|
|output_format|mp3_44100_64|
|output_format|mp3_44100_96|
|output_format|mp3_44100_128|
|output_format|mp3_44100_192|
|output_format|pcm_8000|
|output_format|pcm_16000|
|output_format|pcm_22050|
|output_format|pcm_24000|
|output_format|pcm_32000|
|output_format|pcm_44100|
|output_format|pcm_48000|
|output_format|ulaw_8000|
|output_format|alaw_8000|
|output_format|opus_48000_32|
|output_format|opus_48000_64|
|output_format|opus_48000_96|
|output_format|opus_48000_128|
|output_format|opus_48000_192|
|» model_id|music_v1|
|» model_id|music_v2|
|» model_id|music_v2_5|

<h3 id="video-to-music-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Generated audio file matching the video. Content-Type and file extension depend on the output_format parameter (default mp3).|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Subscription required.|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error (e.g. invalid or missing videos).|None|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|song-id|string||Unique identifier for the generated song|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
    },
```

`POST /v1/studio/podcasts`

Create and auto-convert a podcast project. Currently, the LLM cost is covered by us but you will still be charged for the audio generation. In the future, you will be charged for both the LLM and audio generation costs.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_v2",
  "mode": {
    "conversation": {
      "guest_voice_id": "bYTqZQo3Jz7LQtmGTgwi",
      "host_voice_id": "6lCwbsX1yVjD49QmpkTR"
    },
    "type": "conversation"
  },
  "source": {
    "type": "url",
    "url": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science"
  },
  "quality_preset": "standard",
  "duration_scale": "short",
  "language": "en",
  "intro": "Welcome to the podcast.",
  "outro": "Thank you for listening!",
  "instructions_prompt": "Ensure the podcast remains factual, accurate and appropriate for all audiences.",
  "highlights": [
    "Emphasize the importance of AI on education"
  ],
  "callback_url": [
    "https://www.test.com/my-api/projects-status"
  ],
  "apply_text_normalization": "auto"
}
```

## Create Pronunciation Dictionaries

<a id="opIdupdate_pronunciation_dictionaries"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/studio/projects/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM/pronunciation-dictionaries \
  -X POST \

    "pronunciation_dictionary_locators": [

    ],
    "invalidate_affected_text": false
  }'
```

`POST /v1/studio/projects/{project_id}/pronunciation-dictionaries`

Create a set of pronunciation dictionaries acting on a project. This will automatically mark text within this project as requiring reconverting where the new dictionary would apply or the old one no longer does.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pronunciation_dictionary_locators": [
    "{\"pronunciation_dictionary_id\": \"21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM\", \"version_id\": \"BdF0s0aZ3oFoKnDYdTox\"}"
  ],
  "invalidate_affected_text": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-pronunciation-dictionaries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string|true|The ID of the Studio project.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Create_Pronunciation_Dictionaries_v1_studio_projects__project_id__pronunciation_dictionaries_post](#schemabody_create_pronunciation_dictionaries_v1_studio_projects__project_id__pronunciation_dictionaries_post)|true|none|
|» pronunciation_dictionary_locators|body|[[PronunciationDictionaryVersionLocatorDBModel](#schemapronunciationdictionaryversionlocatordbmodel)]|true|A list of pronunciation dictionary locators (pronunciation_dictionary_id, version_id) encoded as a list of JSON strings for pronunciation dictionaries to be applied to the text. A list of json encoded strings is required as adding projects may occur through formData as opposed to jsonBody. To specify multiple dictionaries use multiple --form lines in your curl, such as --form 'pronunciation_dictionary_locators="{\"pronunciation_dictionary_id\":\"Vmd4Zor6fplcA7WrINey\",\"version_id\":\"hRPaxjlTdR7wFMhV4w0b\"}"' --form 'pronunciation_dictionary_locators="{\"pronunciation_dictionary_id\":\"JzWtcGQMJ6bnlWwyMo7e\",\"version_id\":\"lbmwxiLu4q6txYxgdZqn\"}"'.|
|» invalidate_affected_text|body|boolean|false|This will automatically mark text in this project for reconversion when the new dictionary applies or the old one no longer does.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "status": "ok"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

`POST /v1/studio/projects`

Creates a new Studio project, it can be either initialized as blank, from a document or from a URL.

|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

## List Agents

<a id="opIdget_agents_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/convai/agents`

Returns a list of your agents and their metadata.

<h3 id="list-agents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|How many Agents to return at maximum. Can not exceed 100, defaults to 30.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Search by agents name.|
|archived|query|boolean \| null|false|Filter agents by archived status|
|show_only_owned_agents|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If set to true, the endpoint will omit any agents that were shared with you by someone else and include only the ones you own. Deprecated: use created_by_user_id instead.|
|created_by_user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter agents by creator user ID. When set, only agents created by this user are returned. Takes precedence over show_only_owned_agents. Use '@me' to refer to the authenticated user.|
|tags|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter agents by tag. Repeat the parameter to match any of several tags.|
|sort_direction|query|[SortDirection](#schemasortdirection)|false|The direction to sort the results|
|sort_by|query|[AgentSortBy](#schemaagentsortby) \| null|false|The field to sort the results by|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

## Duplicate Agent

<a id="opIdduplicate_agent_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/agent_3701k3ttaq12ewp8b7qv5rfyszkz/duplicate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "My agent"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/duplicate`

Create a new agent by duplicating an existing one. The new agent gets a copy of every unarchived branch of the source agent, each with the same name and description and starting from the latest version on that branch. The live traffic split is copied onto the new branches, with any share held by a branch that was not copied moved to main. Version history, drafts, archived branches, past traffic splits and experiments are not copied.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My agent"
}
```

<h3 id="duplicate-agent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|string|true|The id of an agent. This is returned on agent creation.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Duplicate_Agent_v1_convai_agents__agent_id__duplicate_post](#schemabody_duplicate_agent_v1_convai_agents__agent_id__duplicate_post)|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|A name to make the agent easier to find|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "agent_id": "J3Pbu5gP6NNKBscdCdwB"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/convai/conversations`

Get all conversations of agents that user owns. With option to restrict to a specific agent.

<h3 id="get-conversations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|agent_id|query|string \| null|false|Agent id (agent_…) or speech engine external id (seng_), resolved to the same underlying resource.|
|visited_agent_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations where any of these agents participated. Can not exceed 50 values.|
|visited_agent_branch_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations where any of these agent branches participated. Can not exceed 50 values.|
|triggered_procedure_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations where any of these procedures were triggered. Can not exceed 50 values.|
|call_successful|query|[EvaluationResultFilter](#schemaevaluationresultfilter) \| null|false|The result of the success evaluation|
|call_start_before_unix|query|integer \| null|false|Unix timestamp (in seconds) to filter conversations up to this start date.|
|call_start_after_unix|query|integer \| null|false|Unix timestamp (in seconds) to filter conversations after to this start date.|
|call_duration_min_secs|query|integer \| null|false|Minimum call duration in seconds.|
|call_duration_max_secs|query|integer \| null|false|Maximum call duration in seconds.|
|rating_max|query|integer \| null|false|Maximum overall rating (1-5).|
|rating_min|query|integer \| null|false|Minimum overall rating (1-5).|
|has_feedback_comment|query|boolean \| null|false|Filter conversations with user feedback comments.|
|user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter conversations by the user ID who initiated them.|
|evaluation_params|query|[string] \| null|false|Evaluation filters. Repeat param. Format: criteria_id:result where result is one of success\|failure\|unknown. Example: eval=value_framing:success|
|data_collection_params|query|[string] \| null|false|Data collection filters. Repeat param. Format: id:op:value where op is one of eq\|neq\|gt\|gte\|lt\|lte\|in. For in, pipe-delimit values. An empty value matches conversations where the field was not collected (id:eq:), and neq with an empty value matches where it was (id:neq:). eq is exact equality. gt\|gte\|lt\|lte require a numeric value.|
|dynamic_variable_params|query|[string] \| null|false|Dynamic variable filters. Repeat param. Format: name:op:value where op is one of eq\|neq\|gt\|gte\|lt\|lte\|in. For in, pipe-delimit values. An empty value matches conversations where the variable was not set (name:eq:), and neq with an empty value matches where it was (name:neq:). eq is exact equality. gt\|gte\|lt\|lte require a numeric value. Names containing ':' cannot be expressed.|
|data_collection_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Data collection field IDs to include in each conversation summary. Repeat param. When omitted, data_collection_results is not returned.|
|evaluation_criteria_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Evaluation criteria IDs to include in each conversation summary. Repeat param. When omitted, evaluation_criteria_results is not returned.|
|tool_names|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by tool names used during the call.|
|tool_names_successful|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by tool names that had successful calls.|
|tool_names_errored|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by tool names that had errored calls.|
|include_invalid_tool_calls|query|boolean|false|Also match tool calls that never ran.|
|main_languages|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by detected main language (language code).|
|page_size|query|integer|false|How many conversations to return at maximum. Can not exceed 100, defaults to 30.|
|summary_mode|query|string|false|Whether to include transcript summaries in the response.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Full-text or fuzzy search over transcript messages|
|conversation_initiation_source|query|[ConversationInitiationSource](#schemaconversationinitiationsource) \| null|false|none|
|text_only|query|boolean \| null|false|none|
|conversation_product_type|query|[ConversationProduct](#schemaconversationproduct) \| null|false|Restrict results to a single conversation product surface.|
|branch_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter conversations by branch ID.|
|version_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter conversations by version ID.|
|parent_conversation_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter conversations by parent conversation ID for subagent conversations.|
|topic_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by topic IDs assigned during topic discovery.|
|exclude_statuses|query|[string] \| null|false|Exclude conversations with the given statuses. Useful for hiding in-progress / processing conversations from list views.|
|tag_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by conversation tag IDs assigned via the conversation-tags endpoints.|
|workflow_node_entered_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter conversations to only those that entered the given node.|
|termination_reasons|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by their stored termination_reason (metadata.termination_reason). Repeat param to match any of several.|
|guardrail_types|query|[[GuardrailType](#schemaguardrailtype)] \| null|false|Filter to conversations where a guardrail of any of these types triggered (metadata.triggered_guardrails.guardrail_type). Repeat param to match any of several.|
|custom_guardrail_names|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter to conversations where a custom guardrail with any of these names triggered (metadata.triggered_guardrails.guardrail_name). Only custom guardrails carry a name. Repeat param to match any of several.|
|sort_direction|query|[SortDirection](#schemasortdirection)|false|The direction to sort conversations by call start time. Defaults to descending (newest first).|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|summary_mode|exclude|
|summary_mode|include|
|sort_direction|asc|
|sort_direction|desc|

## Get Conversation Summary

<a id="opIdget_conversation_summary_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/conversations/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM/summary \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/convai/conversations/{conversation_id}/summary`

Get a lightweight summary of a conversation: its title, the generated transcript summary, whether the call was successful, and — only when the conversation is short — the plain chat messages. Tool calls, tool results, and contextual updates are omitted so the response stays small. Use this instead of the full conversation endpoint when you only need the gist (e.g. an agent reading many conversations); use GET /v1/convai/conversations/{conversation_id} when you need the full transcript with tool calls and contextual updates.

<h3 id="get-conversation-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|conversation_id|path|string|true|The id of the conversation you're taking the action on.|
|max_messages|query|integer|false|Maximum number of chat message turns to include inline. When the conversation has more than this, the messages are omitted and messages_omitted is set.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "string",
  "agent_id": "string",
  "status": "initiated",
  "call_summary_title": "string",
  "transcript_summary": "string",
  "call_successful": "success",
  "message_count": 0,
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages_omitted": false,
  "note": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|text_query|query|string|true|The search query text for full-text and fuzzy matching|
|agent_id|query|string \| null|false|Agent id (agent_…) or speech engine external id (seng_), resolved to the same underlying resource.|
|visited_agent_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations where any of these agents participated. Can not exceed 50 values.|
|visited_agent_branch_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations where any of these agent branches participated. Can not exceed 50 values.|
|triggered_procedure_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations where any of these procedures were triggered. Can not exceed 50 values.|
|call_successful|query|[EvaluationResultFilter](#schemaevaluationresultfilter) \| null|false|The result of the success evaluation|
|call_start_before_unix|query|integer \| null|false|Unix timestamp (in seconds) to filter conversations up to this start date.|
|call_start_after_unix|query|integer \| null|false|Unix timestamp (in seconds) to filter conversations after to this start date.|
|call_duration_min_secs|query|integer \| null|false|Minimum call duration in seconds.|
|call_duration_max_secs|query|integer \| null|false|Maximum call duration in seconds.|
|rating_max|query|integer \| null|false|Maximum overall rating (1-5).|
|rating_min|query|integer \| null|false|Minimum overall rating (1-5).|
|has_feedback_comment|query|boolean \| null|false|Filter conversations with user feedback comments.|
|user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter conversations by the user ID who initiated them.|
|evaluation_params|query|[string] \| null|false|Evaluation filters. Repeat param. Format: criteria_id:result where result is one of success\|failure\|unknown. Example: eval=value_framing:success|
|data_collection_params|query|[string] \| null|false|Data collection filters. Repeat param. Format: id:op:value where op is one of eq\|neq\|gt\|gte\|lt\|lte\|in. For in, pipe-delimit values. An empty value matches conversations where the field was not collected (id:eq:), and neq with an empty value matches where it was (id:neq:). eq is exact equality. gt\|gte\|lt\|lte require a numeric value.|
|dynamic_variable_params|query|[string] \| null|false|Dynamic variable filters. Repeat param. Format: name:op:value where op is one of eq\|neq\|gt\|gte\|lt\|lte\|in. For in, pipe-delimit values. An empty value matches conversations where the variable was not set (name:eq:), and neq with an empty value matches where it was (name:neq:). eq is exact equality. gt\|gte\|lt\|lte require a numeric value. Names containing ':' cannot be expressed.|
|tool_names|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by tool names used during the call.|
|tool_names_successful|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by tool names that had successful calls.|
|tool_names_errored|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by tool names that had errored calls.|
|include_invalid_tool_calls|query|boolean|false|Also match tool calls that never ran.|
|main_languages|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by detected main language (language code).|
|exclude_statuses|query|[string] \| null|false|Exclude conversations with the given statuses. Useful for hiding in-progress / processing conversations from list views.|
|termination_reasons|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by their stored termination_reason (metadata.termination_reason). Repeat param to match any of several.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of results per page. Max 50.|
|summary_mode|query|string|false|Whether to include transcript summaries in the response.|
|conversation_initiation_source|query|[ConversationInitiationSource](#schemaconversationinitiationsource) \| null|false|none|
|text_only|query|boolean \| null|false|none|
|conversation_product_type|query|[ConversationProduct](#schemaconversationproduct) \| null|false|Restrict results to a single conversation product surface.|
|branch_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter conversations by branch ID.|
|version_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter conversations by version ID.|
|topic_ids|query|[string] \| null|false|Filter conversations by topic IDs assigned during topic discovery.|
|sort_by|query|[MessageSearchSortBy](#schemamessagesearchsortby)|false|Sort order for search results. 'search_score' sorts by search score, 'created_at' sorts by conversation start time.|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|summary_mode|exclude|
|summary_mode|include|
|sort_by|search_score|
|sort_by|created_at|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|branch_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter by assigned branch ID|

|sort_direction|query|[SortDirection](#schemasortdirection)|false|The direction to sort the results|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|created_by_user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter documents by creator user ID. When set, only documents created by this user are returned. Takes precedence over show_only_owned_documents. Use '@me' to refer to the authenticated user.|
|types|query|[[KnowledgeBaseDocumentType](#schemaknowledgebasedocumenttype)] \| null|false|If present, the endpoint will return only documents of the given types.|
|parent_folder_id|query|string \| null|false|If set, the endpoint will return only documents that are direct children of the given folder.|
|ancestor_folder_id|query|string \| null|false|If set, the endpoint will return only documents that are descendants of the given folder.|
|folders_first|query|boolean|false|Whether folders should be returned first in the list of documents.|
|sort_direction|query|[SortDirection](#schemasortdirection)|false|The direction to sort the results|
|sort_by|query|[KnowledgeBaseSortBy](#schemaknowledgebasesortby) \| null|false|The field to sort the results by|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

```json
  "name": "string",
```

```bash
  "auto_remove": true,
```

```json
}
```

<h3 id="update-document-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|[Body_Update_document_v1_convai_knowledge_base__documentation_id__patch](#schemabody_update_document_v1_convai_knowledge_base__documentation_id__patch)|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|A custom, human-readable name for the document.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» content|body|string \| null|false|Updated content for the document. Only supported for text documents, URL documents with auto-sync disabled, and file documents that are not synced from an external source.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» enable_auto_sync|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the document or folder is refreshed automatically. Only applicable to URL documents, folders, and externally-synced files. Leave unset to keep the current value.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» auto_remove|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to automatically remove the document once its source is no longer available. Only applicable when auto-sync is enabled. Leave unset to keep the current value.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» minimum_frequency_days|body|integer \| null|false|Minimum frequency (in days) at which the document is refreshed. The actual interval may be shorter, never longer. Only applicable when auto-sync is enabled. Leave unset to keep the current value.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» tighten_only|body|boolean|false|Folders only. When true, items already in the folder are only tightened to stay at least as strict as the folder, and keep any setting that is stricter than the folder's. When false, they are set to exactly the folder's auto-sync settings. Ignored for externally synced folders, whose contents always follow the folder's schedule.|

## Query Agent Knowledge Base Rag

<a id="opIdquery_agent_knowledge_base_rag_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/agent_3701k3ttaq12ewp8b7qv5rfyszkz/knowledge-base/rag-query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "How do I reset my password?",
    "use_agent_defaults": true,
    "max_documents_length": 1,
    "max_retrieved_rag_chunks_count": 1
  }'
```

`POST /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/knowledge-base/rag-query`

Run the agent's exact RAG retrieval for an ad-hoc query and return the ranked chunks the agent would retrieve. Read-only: no conversation is created. The response reflects current retrieval internals and may evolve.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "query": "How do I reset my password?",
  "use_agent_defaults": true,
  "max_documents_length": 1,
  "max_retrieved_rag_chunks_count": 1
}
```

<h3 id="query-agent-knowledge-base-rag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|string|true|The id of an agent. This is returned on agent creation.|
|branch_id|query|string \| null|false|The ID of the branch to use|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[AgentKnowledgeBaseRagQueryRequestModel](#schemaagentknowledgebaseragqueryrequestmodel)|true|none|
|» query|body|string|true|Query to run against the agent's knowledge base RAG index.|
|» use_agent_defaults|body|boolean|false|When true (the default), retrieval uses the agent's own RAG settings, reproducing exactly what the agent would retrieve. Set to false to retrieve with neutral default RAG settings instead (the agent's embedding model is always kept, since it determines which vector index exists). Useful for auditing the knowledge base independently of how a particular agent is tuned.|
|» max_documents_length|body|integer \| null|false|Optional maximum total character length of document chunks returned. Overrides the selected RAG settings for this query only.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## Create A Merge Proposal

<a id="opIdcreate_merge_proposal_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/agent_3701k3ttaq12ewp8b7qv5rfyszkz/merge-proposals \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "source_branch_id": "string",
    "target_branch_id": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "description": "",
    "requested_reviewer_user_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "triage_ticket_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/merge-proposals`

Record a request to merge a source branch into a target branch. Anyone with edit access can open one; merging it later is gated on write access to the target branch, so this is how a change reaches a protected branch the author cannot merge into themselves.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "source_branch_id": "string",
  "target_branch_id": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "description": "",
  "requested_reviewer_user_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "triage_ticket_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-merge-proposal-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|string|true|The id of an agent. This is returned on agent creation.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Create_a_merge_proposal_v1_convai_agents__agent_id__merge_proposals_post](#schemabody_create_a_merge_proposal_v1_convai_agents__agent_id__merge_proposals_post)|true|none|
|» source_branch_id|body|string|true|Branch whose changes should be merged.|
|» target_branch_id|body|string|true|Branch that should receive the changes.|
|» title|body|string|true|Short title for the merge_proposal.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional longer description for reviewers.|
|» requested_reviewer_user_ids|body|[string] \| null|false|User IDs to request a review from.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» triage_ticket_id|body|string \| null|false|Triage ticket of this agent that the merge_proposal resolves. Merging it resolves the ticket if still open.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

```json
  "created_merge_proposal_id": "string"
}
```

```json
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

`GET /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}/procedures`

## Legacy: Compile Procedures

<a id="opIdcompile_procedures_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/agent_3701k3ttaq12ewp8b7qv5rfyszkz/branches/agtbranch_0901k4aafjxxfxt93gd841r7tv5t/procedures/compile \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}/procedures/compile`

Legacy. Do not use. Saving an agent draft (`POST /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/drafts`) and publishing an agent (`PATCH /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}`) compile structured procedures into workflow nodes and edges, save the compiled workflow with the draft or version, and return validation errors, so a separate compile call is no longer needed. This endpoint remains available for the time being so existing callers do not break, as a dry-run that compiles the current procedure drafts into a workflow without persisting anything. It will eventually be deprecated.

<h3 id="legacy-compile-procedures-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|string|true|Agent ID to get the procedure draft from|
|branch_id|path|string|true|Branch ID to get the procedure draft from|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "workflow": {
    "edges": [],
    "nodes": []
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": {
    "agtprc_6qbpwdq8n01bxhk44bgjy6f10ck3": [
      {
        "message": "Field required",
        "path": "steps.0.message"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Delete Environment Variable

<a id="opIddelete_environment_variable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/environment-variables/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /v1/convai/environment-variables/{env_var_id}`

Delete an environment variable and its values in all environments. WARNING: Agents are not checked. A variable that an agent still uses (custom LLM, webhooks or cloud storage export, on any branch or version) is deleted anyway, and that agent's conversations then fail. The delete is only rejected while tools, MCP servers or the workspace conversation initiation webhook use the variable.

<h3 id="delete-environment-variable-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|env_var_id|path|string|true|none|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

> Example responses

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-environment-variable-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Environment variable deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|Environment variable not found|None|
|409|Conflict|Environment variable is still in use|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<h1 id="elevenlabs-api-documentation-agents-insights">Agents Insights</h1>

Query analytics and insights about agent conversations and performance.

## Get Agent Conversation Topics

<a id="opIdget_agent_topics_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/string/topics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/topics`

Returns the latest topic discovery run results for a given agent.

<h3 id="get-agent-conversation-topics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|string|true|ID of the agent|
|page_size|query|integer \| null|false|Number of top-level topic groups to return.|
|sort_by|query|[TopicSortBy](#schematopicsortby)|false|Column to rank topics by. Use conversations for volume, sentiment with sort_direction=asc for the most negative topics, and frustration with sort_direction=desc for the most frustrated ones. Topics with no score are always ranked last.|
|sort_direction|query|[SortDirection](#schemasortdirection)|false|Direction to sort topics.|
|from_unix_secs|query|integer \| null|false|Start of the window to view topics for. When set with to_unix_secs, the completed daily topic-discovery runs in the range are aggregated together, so the window scopes the metrics as well as the topic set. Floored to the start of its UTC day because runs cover whole UTC days; aggregated_run_count reports how many runs were summed. Omit both bounds to get the single latest run.|
|to_unix_secs|query|integer \| null|false|End of the window to view topics for.|
|include_evaluation_criteria|query|boolean|false|Include the per-criteria evaluation breakdown on each topic's metrics. Pass false to drop it: it dominates the payload and the weighted success_rate is returned either way.|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_by|conversations|
|sort_by|sentiment|
|sort_by|success_rate|
|sort_by|frustration|
|sort_direction|asc|
|sort_direction|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "topics": [
    {
      "topic_id": "string",
      "label": "string",
```

`POST /v1/workspace/analytics/query/usage-by-product-over-time`

Returns credit usage broken down by product type over time. The response is a tabular structure with columns, column_types, column_units, and rows. Some id columns also get a display-name column, such as user_label or voice_name, appended after the existing columns.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "start_time": 1577836800000,
  "end_time": 1577836800000,
  "interval_seconds": 60,
  "group_by": [
    "product_type"
  ],
  "filters": [
    {
      "column": "string",
      "operation": "in",
      "values": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "time_zone": "UTC"
}
```

<h3 id="get-workspace-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Get_Workspace_Usage_v1_workspace_analytics_query_usage_by_product_over_time_post](#schemabody_get_workspace_usage_v1_workspace_analytics_query_usage_by_product_over_time_post)|true|none|
|» start_time|body|integer|true|Start of the time range as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Must be at least 2020-01-01.|
|» end_time|body|integer|true|End of the time range as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Must be at least 2020-01-01.|
|» interval_seconds|body|integer|false|Bucket size in seconds. Each row in the response covers this many seconds of the selected time range. For example, pass 3600 for hourly buckets, 86400 for daily buckets, or 604800 for weekly buckets. Whether `time_zone` shifts bucket boundaries depends on this value: week multiples (e.g. 604800) are calendar weeks that start Monday at local midnight; whole-day multiples that are not whole weeks (e.g. 86400) align to local midnight; whole-hour multiples up to 24 hours (e.g. 3600, 14400) align to local hour boundaries from midnight; sub-hour values and other sizes remain UTC-anchored regardless of `time_zone`.|
|» group_by|body|[string] \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» filters|body|[[ColumnFilter](#schemacolumnfilter)] \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[[ColumnFilter](#schemacolumnfilter)]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» time_zone|body|string|false|IANA time zone identifier (e.g. 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'UTC') used to align bucket boundaries for eligible `interval_seconds` values. Week multiples (e.g. 604800) are calendar weeks that start Monday at local midnight. Whole-day multiples that are not whole weeks start at local midnight; whole-hour multiples up to 24 hours align to local hour boundaries from midnight. Sub-hour intervals and other bucket sizes remain UTC-anchored regardless of this setting. Defaults to UTC.|

`POST /v1/workspace/analytics/requests`

Returns a list of API requests. Supports filtering by time range, column filters, and search terms. At least one of start_time or end_time must be provided. An optional sort parameter controls timestamp ordering. Results are ordered by timestamp. Descending if end_time is used, ascending if start_time is used. The response is a tabular structure with columns, column_types, column_units, and rows.

```json
  "start_time": 1577836800000,
  "end_time": 1577836800000,
  "limit": 100,
  "sort": "asc",
  "filters": [
```

## Get Characters Usage Metrics (Deprecated)

<a id="opIdusage_characters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/usage/character-stats?start_unix=1685574000&end_unix=1688165999' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/usage/character-stats`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

(Deprecated) This endpoint is deprecated. Use /v1/workspace/analytics/query/usage-by-product-over-time instead, which exposes the bucket size as `interval_seconds` (an integer in seconds) rather than `aggregation_interval`. Returns the usage metrics for the current user or the entire workspace they are part of. The response provides a time axis based on the specified aggregation interval (default: day), with usage values for each interval along that axis. Usage is broken down by the selected breakdown type. For example, breakdown type "voice" will return the usage of each voice for each interval along the time axis.

<h3 id="get-characters-usage-metrics-deprecated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_unix|query|integer|true|UTC Unix timestamp for the start of the usage window, in milliseconds. To include the first day of the window, the timestamp should be at 00:00:00 of that day.|
|end_unix|query|integer|true|UTC Unix timestamp for the end of the usage window, in milliseconds. To include the last day of the window, the timestamp should be at 23:59:59 of that day.|
|include_workspace_metrics|query|boolean|false|Whether or not to include the statistics of the entire workspace.|
|breakdown_type|query|[BreakdownTypes](#schemabreakdowntypes)|false|How to break down the information. Cannot be "user" if include_workspace_metrics is False.|
|aggregation_interval|query|[UsageAggregationInterval](#schemausageaggregationinterval)|false|How to aggregate usage data over time. Can be "hour", "day", "week", "month", or "cumulative".|
|aggregation_bucket_size|query|integer \| null|false|Aggregation bucket size in seconds. Overrides the aggregation interval.|
|metric|query|[MetricType](#schemametrictype)|false|Which metric to aggregate.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|breakdown_type|none|
|breakdown_type|voice|
|breakdown_type|voice_multiplier|
|breakdown_type|user|
|breakdown_type|groups|
|breakdown_type|api_keys|
|breakdown_type|all_api_keys|
|breakdown_type|product_type|
|breakdown_type|model|
|breakdown_type|resource|
|breakdown_type|request_queue|
|breakdown_type|region|
|breakdown_type|subresource_id|
|breakdown_type|reporting_workspace_id|
|breakdown_type|has_api_key|
|breakdown_type|request_source|
|aggregation_interval|hour|
|aggregation_interval|day|
|aggregation_interval|week|
|aggregation_interval|month|
|aggregation_interval|cumulative|
|metric|credits|
|metric|tts_characters|
|metric|minutes_used|
|metric|request_count|
|metric|ttfb_avg|
|metric|ttfb_p95|
|metric|fiat_units_spent|
|metric|concurrency|
|metric|concurrency_average|

## List Agent Response Tests

<a id="opIdlist_chat_response_tests_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agent-testing \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/convai/agent-testing`

Lists all agent response tests with pagination support and optional search filtering.

<h3 id="list-agent-response-tests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|How many Tests to return at maximum. Can not exceed 100, defaults to 30.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Search query to filter tests and folders by name.|
|parent_folder_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter by parent folder ID. Use 'root' to get items in the root folder.|
|types|query|[[TestType](#schematesttype)] \| null|false|If present, the endpoint will return only tests/folders of the given types.|
|include_folders|query|boolean \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Use the `types` query param and include `folder` instead.|
|sort_mode|query|string|false|Sort mode for listing tests. Use 'folders_first' to place folders before tests.|
|sharing_mode|query|[TestSharingMode](#schematestsharingmode)|false|Filter test visibility. Use `shared_with_me` to return only tests/folders shared with the current user that they did not create.|
|created_by_user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter tests and folders by creator user ID. Use '@me' to refer to the authenticated user.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_mode|default|
|sort_mode|folders_first|
|sharing_mode|all|
|sharing_mode|shared_with_me|

```json
    {

        {
          "id": "string",

        }
      ],

    }
  ],
```

`GET /v1/convai/test-invocations`

Lists all test invocations with pagination support and optional search filtering.

<h3 id="list-test-invocations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|agent_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter by agent ID|
|branch_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter by branch ID|
|test_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter to invocations that include a run of this test id|
|start_time|query|integer \| null|false|Inclusive lower bound on created_at, in unix seconds|
|end_time|query|integer \| null|false|Inclusive upper bound on created_at, in unix seconds|
|version_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter by the agent version the tests ran against|
|page_size|query|integer|false|How many Tests to return at maximum. Can not exceed 100, defaults to 30.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Search query to filter tests and folders by name.|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

<h3 id="run-tests-on-the-agent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|string|true|The id of an agent. This is returned on agent creation.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[RunAgentTestsRequestModel](#schemarunagenttestsrequestmodel)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|Optional name for the test invocation.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» tests|body|[[SingleTestRunRequestModel](#schemasingletestrunrequestmodel)]|true|List of tests to run on the agent|
|» agent_config_override|body|[AdhocAgentConfigOverrideForTestRequestModel](#schemaadhocagentconfigoverridefortestrequestmodel) \| null|false|Configuration overrides to use for testing. If not provided, the agent's default configuration will be used.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AdhocAgentConfigOverrideForTestRequestModel](#schemaadhocagentconfigoverridefortestrequestmodel)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» branch_id|body|string \| null|false|ID of the branch to run the tests on. If not provided, the tests will be run on the agent's main branch.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» repeat_count|body|integer|false|Number of times to run each test. When greater than 1, results are grouped and summarized.|

## Get Test Invocation

<a id="opIdget_test_invocation_route"></a>

> Code samples

`GET /v1/convai/test-invocations/{test_invocation_id}`

Gets a test invocation by ID.

|---|---|---|---|---|

## Update Test Invocation

<a id="opIdupdate_test_invocation_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/test-invocations/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/convai/test-invocations/{test_invocation_id}`

Updates the user-provided name of a test invocation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-test-invocation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|test_invocation_id|path|string|true|The id of a test invocation. This is returned when tests are run.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[UpdateTestSuiteInvocationRequestModel](#schemaupdatetestsuiteinvocationrequestmodel)|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|true|New name for the test invocation. Set to null to restore the generated title.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## Cancel Test Invocation

<a id="opIdcancel_test_invocation_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/test-invocations/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /v1/convai/test-invocations/{test_invocation_id}/cancel`

Cancels all pending runs in a test invocation.

<h3 id="cancel-test-invocation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|test_invocation_id|path|string|true|The id of a test invocation. This is returned when tests are run.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

> Example responses

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="cancel-test-invocation-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Successful Response|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`POST /v1/convai/test-invocations/{test_invocation_id}/resubmit`

Resubmits specific test runs from a test invocation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "test_run_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "agent_config_override": {
```

## List Agent Conversation Tickets

<a id="opIdlist_agent_conversation_tickets_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/string/triage-tickets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/triage-tickets`

List an agent's conversation triage tickets, ordered by most recently created first unless sorted by priority. These are tickets about the agent's own performance on a conversation (for triage with Architect), not tickets an agent opens for end users.

<h3 id="list-agent-conversation-tickets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|string|true|none|
|page_size|query|integer|false|How many agent conversation tickets to return. Can not exceed 100.|
|conversation_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets by conversation id.|
|status|query|[AgentConversationTicketStatus](#schemaagentconversationticketstatus) \| null|false|Filter tickets by status.|
|sources|query|[[AgentConversationTicketSource](#schemaagentconversationticketsource)] \| null|false|Filter tickets by how they were raised (qa, agent, manual). Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple sources.|
|priorities|query|[[AgentConversationTicketPriority](#schemaagentconversationticketpriority)] \| null|false|Filter tickets by priority. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple priorities.|
|sort_by|query|[AgentConversationTicketSortBy](#schemaagentconversationticketsortby)|false|Order by most recently created, or by priority (most urgent first, then most recently created).|
|owner_user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets by creator. Use 'agent' for agent-raised tickets.|
|assignee_user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets by assignee. Use 'unassigned' for tickets with no assignee.|
|issue_type|query|[AgentConversationTicketIssueType](#schemaagentconversationticketissuetype) \| null|false|Filter clusters by issue type.|
|label|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets by an exact label.|
|merged_into_ticket_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets merged into this ticket.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Case-insensitive free-text search across the ticket's title, description, comments, and turn comments.|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_by|created_at|
|sort_by|priority|

## Create Manual Agent Ticket

<a id="opIdcreate_manual_agent_ticket_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/string/triage-tickets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "string",
    "qa_comment": "string",
    "priority": "low"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/triage-tickets`

Manually raise a follow-up ticket against an agent, not tied to any conversation (for example a task like 'add the KB about X'). Without a title, one is derived from the comment. Requires viewer access to the agent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "string",
  "qa_comment": "string",
  "priority": "low"
}
```

<h3 id="create-manual-agent-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_id|path|string|true|none|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[CreateManualTicketRequestModel](#schemacreatemanualticketrequestmodel)|true|none|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|One-line headline shown in the triage list. Defaults to one derived from qa_comment.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» qa_comment|body|string|true|What the ticket is about, e.g. a follow-up task for the agent.|
|» priority|body|[AgentConversationTicketPriority](#schemaagentconversationticketpriority) \| null|false|How urgently the ticket needs attention.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AgentConversationTicketPriority](#schemaagentconversationticketpriority)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|low|
|» » *anyOf*|medium|
|» » *anyOf*|high|
|» » *anyOf*|urgent|

## List Workspace Conversation Tickets

<a id="opIdlist_workspace_conversation_tickets_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/triage-tickets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/convai/triage-tickets`

List conversation triage tickets across every agent in the workspace, ordered by most recently created first. Use this to build a workspace-wide view (for example, tickets assigned to the caller). Supports the same filters, sorting and search as the per-agent endpoint. Tickets for agents the caller cannot access are omitted.

<h3 id="list-workspace-conversation-tickets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|How many agent conversation tickets to return. Can not exceed 100.|
|agent_id|query|string \| null|false|Only tickets for this agent.|
|status|query|[AgentConversationTicketStatus](#schemaagentconversationticketstatus) \| null|false|Filter tickets by status.|
|sources|query|[[AgentConversationTicketSource](#schemaagentconversationticketsource)] \| null|false|Filter tickets by how they were raised (qa, agent, manual). Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple sources.|
|priorities|query|[[AgentConversationTicketPriority](#schemaagentconversationticketpriority)] \| null|false|Filter tickets by priority. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple priorities.|
|sort_by|query|[AgentConversationTicketSortBy](#schemaagentconversationticketsortby)|false|Order by most recently created, or by priority (most urgent first, then most recently created).|
|owner_user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets by creator. Use 'agent' for agent-raised tickets.|
|assignee_user_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets by assignee. Use 'unassigned' for tickets with no assignee.|
|issue_type|query|[AgentConversationTicketIssueType](#schemaagentconversationticketissuetype) \| null|false|Filter clusters by issue type.|
|label|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets by an exact label.|
|merged_into_ticket_id|query|string \| null|false|Filter tickets merged into this ticket.|
|search|query|string \| null|false|Case-insensitive free-text search across the ticket's title, description, comments, and turn comments.|
|cursor|query|string \| null|false|Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|sort_by|created_at|
|sort_by|priority|

## Create Agent Conversation Ticket

<a id="opIdcreate_agent_conversation_ticket_route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/triage-tickets \

        "comment": "string"
      }
    ],
    "priority": "low"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/convai/triage-tickets`

Raise a ticket about an agent's performance on a conversation, for triage with Architect. Provide an overall comment and/or turn-level comments describing what went wrong.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "qa_comment": "string",
  "turn_comments": [
    {
      "turn_index": 0,
      "comment": "string"
    }
  ],
  "priority": "low"
}
```

<h3 id="create-agent-conversation-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[CreateAgentConversationTicketRequestModel](#schemacreateagentconversationticketrequestmodel)|true|none|
|» conversation_id|body|string|true|Conversation this ticket is about.|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|One-line headline shown in the triage list. Defaults to one derived from the comments, falling back to the conversation's summary title. Ignored when the comment is added to the conversation's open ticket.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» qa_comment|body|string \| null|false|The issue this ticket is about, covering the whole conversation rather than a single turn.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» turn_comments|body|[[TurnCommentRequestModel](#schematurncommentrequestmodel)]|false|Optional turn-level comments on what went wrong.|
|» priority|body|[AgentConversationTicketPriority](#schemaagentconversationticketpriority) \| null|false|How urgently the ticket needs attention. If the conversation already has an open ticket, it is raised to this priority when lower.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AgentConversationTicketPriority](#schemaagentconversationticketpriority)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

## Create Dubbing Project

<a id="opIddubbing_project_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/dubbing/project \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -F 'file=string' \
  -F 'source_url=string' \
  -F 'reference=string' \
  -F 'source_language=string' \
  -F 'model_id=dubbing_v1' \
  -F 'keyterms=["string"]' \
  -F 'webhook_ids=["string"]' \
  -F 'target_language=string' \
  -F 'transcript=string'
```

`POST /v1/dubbing/project`

Create a dubbing project from an uploaded file (`file`) or a source URL (`source_url`).

Returns as soon as the project record exists, before the source has been fetched: the project starts `queued` and reaches `ready` once its source has been transcribed. Add a language target to it for each language you want, or pass `target_language` to queue the first one here.

Creating a project incurs a minimum charge of one language: you are charged for at least one language's dubbing when the project is created, before any output exists. This charge prepays the first language target — the first target you add, or the one queued via `target_language`, consumes it — and each additional language is charged separately.

Preparation can take minutes on a long source, so we recommend passing `webhook_ids` to be notified when the project turns `ready` or `failed`, rather than polling for it.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
source_url: string
reference: string
source_language: string
model_id: dubbing_v1
keyterms:
  - string
webhook_ids:
  - string
target_language: string
transcript: string
```

<h3 id="create-dubbing-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Create_Dubbing_Project_v1_dubbing_project_post](#schemabody_create_dubbing_project_v1_dubbing_project_post)|false|none|
|» file|body|string(binary) \| null|false|The source media file to dub: an audio or video file of at most 3 GiB. Provide this or `source_url`, not both.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» source_url|body|string \| null|false|Public HTTP(S) URL the source media is fetched from server-side, subject to the same size and format limits as an upload. Provide this or `file`, not both.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» reference|body|string \| null|false|Optional free-form string (at most 500 characters) to identify the project on your end. Stored and echoed back verbatim; it does not affect the dub.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» source_language|body|string \| null|false|BCP-47 language tag of the source media; must be a language the transcription model supports. Any region or script subtag is ignored, since transcription is per-language. Omit to auto-detect.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» model_id|body|string \| null|false|Dubbing model (`dubbing_v1` or `dubbing_v2`) every language target of this project is dubbed with. Defaults to `dubbing_v2`. Fixed at create time — the source is prepared for this model, so neither the project nor an individual target can change it later.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» keyterms|body|[string]|false|Key terms to bias transcription and translation toward (for example, product or brand names). At most 1,000 terms; each term at most 50 characters and 5 words; the characters `<>{}[]\` are not allowed. Terms are trimmed and deduplicated. Repeat the field once per term, or pass a single JSON array.|
|» webhook_ids|body|[string]|false|IDs of workspace webhooks to notify as this project progresses — the alternative to polling, and what we recommend. Each receives a `dubbing_project_ready` or `dubbing_project_failed` event for the project, and a `dubbing_language_completed` or `dubbing_language_failed` event for every language under it; `dubbing_language_completed` carries the output download URLs. At most 3 IDs, each already configured in your workspace — see [Webhooks](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/resources/webhooks) for how to create one and verify its signature. Repeat the field once per ID, or pass a single JSON array or comma-separated string. Delivery is best-effort and can repeat, so we recommend handling events idempotently.|
|» target_language|body|string \| null|false|Optional shortcut: also create a language target in this BCP-47 language, queued to start once the project is ready — equivalent to creating the project and then creating one language target. Must be one of the [languages the dubbing model supports](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/dubbing/which-languages-are-supported-in-dubbing), and a region-qualified tag must be one of the supported dialects. This is the first language target, so it consumes the project's minimum charge rather than adding to it. Its ID is returned in `language_ids`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» transcript|body|string(binary) \| null|false|Enterprise only. Optional JSON transcript to use instead of transcribing the source: a `{"segments": [...]}` document, at most 20,000 segments and 4 MiB. See [Bring your own transcript](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/dubbing/bring-your-own-transcript) for the segment fields and their constraints. `source_language` is required whenever a transcript is provided. If any segment carries a `translation`, `target_language` is required and every segment must carry one; those translations seed the target created via `target_language`, which then skips machine translation.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|dubbing_v1|
|» » *anyOf*|dubbing_v2|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "project_id": "string",
  "status": "queued",
  "reference": "string",
  "source_language": "string",
  "model_id": "string",
  "media": {
    "filename": "string",
    "duration_s": 0,
    "has_video": true,
    "mime_type": "string"
  },
  "language_ids": [],
  "webhook_ids": [],
  "revision": 0,
  "error": {
    "code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "retryable": true
  },
  "warnings": [
    {
      "type": "voices_not_permitted",
      "speaker_ids": [
        "string"
      ],
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

```json
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create Dubbing Language Target

<a id="opIddubbing_language_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/dubbing/project/string/language \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "target_language": "string",
    "voice_settings": {
      "cloning_strength": 7
    },
    "translations": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/dubbing/project/{project_id}/language`

Add a language to dub a project into, and queue the dub.

This is the call that produces dubbed audio, and it is billed per generation. The target is created `queued` and starts as soon as the project is `ready`, so it can be added at any point after the project is created. It inherits the project's dubbing model and cannot pick another.

A project created with `webhook_ids` sends a `dubbing_language_completed` event carrying the output download URLs, so we recommend subscribing rather than polling this target to completion.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "target_language": "string",
  "voice_settings": {
    "cloning_strength": 7
  },
  "translations": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-dubbing-language-target-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string|true|Identifier of the parent dubbing project.|
|xi-api-key|header|string \| null|false|Your API key. This is required by most endpoints to access our API programmatically. You can view your xi-api-key using the 'Profile' tab on the website.|
|body|body|[Body_Create_Dubbing_Language_Target_v1_dubbing_project__project_id__language_post](#schemabody_create_dubbing_language_target_v1_dubbing_project__project_id__language_post)|true|none|
|» target_language|body|string|true|BCP-47 language tag to dub the project into (for example, `fr` or `es-MX`). Must be one of the [languages the project's dubbing model supports](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/dubbing/which-languages-are-supported-in-dubbing), and a region-qualified tag must be one of the supported dialects.|
|» voice_settings|body|[VoiceSettings](#schemavoicesettings) \| null|false|Voice settings applied to every speaker in this language. Omit to use the defaults.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[VoiceSettings](#schemavoicesettings)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» translations|body|object \| null|false|Enterprise only. Optional translations to use instead of machine translation. A map from each source segment's `external_id` (or its `id`, if you supplied none) to the translated text; every source segment must be covered exactly once. At most 20,000 entries, totaling at most 4 MiB of text. See [Bring your own transcript](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/dubbing/bring-your-own-transcript).|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "language_id": "string",
  "project_id": "string",
  "target_language": "string",
  "status": "queued",
  "model_id": "string",
  "voice_settings": {
    "cloning_strength": 7
  },
  "outputs": {
    "lossless_audio": "string",
    "subtitles": "string"
  },
  "revision": 0,
  "output_revision": 0,
  "error": {
    "code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "retryable": true
  },
  "warnings": [

      "type": "voices_not_permitted",
      "speaker_ids": [
        "string"
      ],
      "message": "string"
    }
  ],
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```
