<h2 id="tocS_GenerationChunk-Input">GenerationChunk-Input</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemagenerationchunk-input"></a>
<a id="schema_GenerationChunk-Input"></a>
<a id="tocSgenerationchunk-input"></a>
<a id="tocsgenerationchunk-input"></a>

```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "duration_ms": 3000,
  "positive_styles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "negative_styles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "context_adherence": "high",
  "conditioning_ref": {
    "song_id": "string",
    "range": {
      "start_ms": 0,
      "end_ms": 0
    }
  },
  "condition_strength": "low"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|text|string|true|none|The text config to be generated for this chunk. Can contain an optional section name in square brackets at the beginning, e.g. [Verse 1], lyrics lines, and inline directions in curly braces, e.g. {scratching}. Section names must be between 1 and 100 characters. At most 30 lines are allowed, each at most 200 characters.|
|duration_ms|integer|true|none|The duration of the chunk in milliseconds. Must be between 3000ms and 120000ms.|
|positive_styles|[string]|true|none|The styles and musical directions that should be present in this chunk. Use English language for best results. The styles for the first chunk are the most important as they set the overall tone and genre. Styles for subsequent chunks can be used to add nuance, progression, emphasis, or change the direction of the song. Aim to have at least 6-7 styles in early chunks until the direction is established. Generic styles like 'great production quality' are good default styles to append to the list.|
|negative_styles|[string]|false|none|The styles and musical directions that should not be present in this chunk. Use English language for best results. Leaving empty is a good default, only use this field if you want to explicitly avoid a particular style or direction.|
|context_adherence|string|false|none|How much the model adheres to the context of its surrounding chunks. Low adherence means the model can deviate from the context and be more creative. High adherence means the model will be more consistent with the context.|
|conditioning_ref|[AudioRefChunk](#schemaaudiorefchunk) \| null|false|none|The audio reference to condition the generation on. The first chunk is the most important as it will influence the generation of all subsequent chunks. Thus, if you want to apply conditioning to the entire song, start conditioning from the first chunk.|
|condition_strength|[ConditionStrength](#schemaconditionstrength) \| null|false|none|How strongly the model adheres to the conditioning reference. Low strength means the model will be more creative and deviate from the reference. High strength means the model will be more consistent with the reference.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|context_adherence|low|
|context_adherence|medium|
|context_adherence|high|

<h2 id="tocS_GenerationChunk-Output">GenerationChunk-Output</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemagenerationchunk-output"></a>
<a id="schema_GenerationChunk-Output"></a>
<a id="tocSgenerationchunk-output"></a>
<a id="tocsgenerationchunk-output"></a>

```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "duration_ms": 3000,
  "positive_styles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "negative_styles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "context_adherence": "high",
  "conditioning_ref": {
    "song_id": "string",
    "range": {
      "start_ms": 0,
      "end_ms": 0
    }
  },
  "condition_strength": "low"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|text|string|true|none|The text config to be generated for this chunk. Can contain an optional section name in square brackets at the beginning, e.g. [Verse 1], lyrics lines, and inline directions in curly braces, e.g. {scratching}. Section names must be between 1 and 100 characters. At most 30 lines are allowed, each at most 200 characters.|
|duration_ms|integer|true|none|The duration of the chunk in milliseconds. Must be between 3000ms and 120000ms.|
|positive_styles|[string]|true|none|The styles and musical directions that should be present in this chunk. Use English language for best results. The styles for the first chunk are the most important as they set the overall tone and genre. Styles for subsequent chunks can be used to add nuance, progression, emphasis, or change the direction of the song. Aim to have at least 6-7 styles in early chunks until the direction is established. Generic styles like 'great production quality' are good default styles to append to the list.|
|negative_styles|[string]|false|none|The styles and musical directions that should not be present in this chunk. Use English language for best results. Leaving empty is a good default, only use this field if you want to explicitly avoid a particular style or direction.|
|context_adherence|string|false|none|How much the model adheres to the context of its surrounding chunks. Low adherence means the model can deviate from the context and be more creative. High adherence means the model will be more consistent with the context.|
|conditioning_ref|[AudioRefChunk](#schemaaudiorefchunk) \| null|false|none|The audio reference to condition the generation on. The first chunk is the most important as it will influence the generation of all subsequent chunks. Thus, if you want to apply conditioning to the entire song, start conditioning from the first chunk.|
|condition_strength|[ConditionStrength](#schemaconditionstrength) \| null|false|none|How strongly the model adheres to the conditioning reference. Low strength means the model will be more creative and deviate from the reference. High strength means the model will be more consistent with the reference.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|context_adherence|low|
|context_adherence|medium|
|context_adherence|high|

Exit branch taken when the Genesys Bot Connector session ends.

These values are the intent names registered in the Genesys bot list, so they are

```json
{
  "smb_tool_type": "get_agent_config"
}
```

Return the full editable config of a single receptionist, including the
current ``additional_instructions`` text.

``list_customer_facing_agents`` is intentionally lightweight (metadata and a
truncated greeting preview) and omits ``additional_instructions``. Call this
tool whenever you need the current full text before calling
``update_agent_config`` on ``first_message`` or ``additional_instructions``
so you can preserve what is already there.


Look up an appointment by the booking confirmation number the caller quotes.

The confirmation number is the 8-character code shown on the booking
confirmation page (e.g. ``#01ABCDEF``). Callers may read it back with or
without the leading ``#`` and with varied spacing; the tool normalizes
the input and does a prefix match on the stored calendar item id.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|smb_tool_type|string|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_GetWorkspacePlanParams">GetWorkspacePlanParams</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemagetworkspaceplanparams"></a>
<a id="schema_GetWorkspacePlanParams"></a>
<a id="tocSgetworkspaceplanparams"></a>
<a id="tocsgetworkspaceplanparams"></a>

```json
{
  "smb_tool_type": "get_workspace_plan"
}
```

Read the workspace's current Reception plan and its hard limits.

Call this before answering any plan, pricing, trial, or limit question so
the assistant stops guessing (e.g. telling a paying owner they're on the
trial, or hallucinating concurrent-call / receptionist / voice-cloning
caps). The tool exposes only the shape of the plan — a display name;
whether it's trial / paid / untiered; the entitlement caps (max
receptionists, phone numbers, active locations, team members, concurrent
calls, voice-cloning quota) alongside the current counts; and whether
there's a payment issue. It deliberately does NOT return list prices or
dollar amounts, nor the trial / renewal end date: pricing and renewal
dates are a product decision and live in the Settings > Billing plan
picker.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|smb_tool_type|string|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_IngestFailure">IngestFailure</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaingestfailure"></a>
<a id="schema_IngestFailure"></a>
<a id="tocSingestfailure"></a>
<a id="tocsingestfailure"></a>

```json
"blocked_url"
```

Why a run failed, as a bounded taxonomy.

Set explicitly at each raise site rather than recovered from the message
text, so rewording a user-facing string cannot silently reshape the metric.
The ``UPSTREAM_*`` causes are the exception: an unclassified escape is
sorted by its type in ``ScrapeRun.failed``, so a dependency outage (the
agents knowledge-base routes, the sandbox) is not filed as ``UNKNOWN``.

<h2 id="tocS_InlineAudioReference">InlineAudioReference</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainlineaudioreference"></a>
<a id="schema_InlineAudioReference"></a>
<a id="tocSinlineaudioreference"></a>
<a id="tocsinlineaudioreference"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "inline_base64",
  "content_base64": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAA...",
  "mime_type": "audio/mpeg"
}
```

Audio passed inline as base64. The audio is stored as an ephemeral
asset with no guaranteed retention: it may be deleted at any time after
the generation completes. To keep an input and reuse it across
generations, upload it via the assets API (`POST /v1/assets`) and pass
an `asset` reference instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|content_base64|string|true|none|The media file's bytes, base64-encoded (standard alphabet). Up to 25MB decoded.|
|mime_type|string|true|none|The MIME type of the encoded audio.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mime_type|audio/mpeg|
|mime_type|audio/wav|

<h2 id="tocS_KnowledgeSourceStatus">KnowledgeSourceStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaknowledgesourcestatus"></a>
<a id="schema_KnowledgeSourceStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSknowledgesourcestatus"></a>
<a id="tocsknowledgesourcestatus"></a>

```json
"processing"
```

Processing status for knowledge sources.

Simple three-state machine:
- PROCESSING: Any active work (uploading, crawling, extracting, etc.)
- READY: Processing complete, results available
- ERROR: Something went wrong (user can retry)

Detailed progress is tracked via the `progress` field.

```json
{
```

```json
  "fallback_complete_percentage": 100,
  "fallback_start_days": 14,
  "fallback_start_percentage": 25,
  "warning_start_days": 30
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|warning_start_days|integer|true|none|Number of days before the provider deprecation date when warnings start being shown.|
|fallback_start_days|integer|true|none|Number of days before the provider deprecation date when traffic starts being routed to the replacement model.|
|fallback_complete_days|integer|true|none|Number of days before the provider deprecation date when all traffic is routed to the replacement model.|
|fallback_start_percentage|integer|true|none|Percentage of traffic routed to the replacement model when fallback begins.|
|fallback_complete_percentage|integer|true|none|Percentage of traffic routed to the replacement model when fallback is complete.|

<h2 id="tocS_LLMDeprecationInfoModel">LLMDeprecationInfoModel</h2>

```json
{
  "fallback_percentage": 0,
  "is_deprecated": true,
  "is_in_fallback_period": false,
  "is_in_warning_period": true,
  "llm": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "provider_deprecation_date": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",
  "replacement_model": "gpt-4o"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|llm|[LLM](#schemallm)|true|none|The identifier of the deprecated LLM model.|
|is_deprecated|boolean|true|none|Whether this model is currently deprecated. True if the model is immediately deprecated or within the warning period.|
|is_in_warning_period|boolean|false|none|Whether this model is currently in the warning period before deprecation.|
|is_in_fallback_period|boolean|false|none|Whether traffic is currently being progressively routed to the replacement model.|
|fallback_percentage|integer|false|none|Current percentage of traffic being routed to the replacement model (0-100).|
|provider_deprecation_date|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The date when the model provider will deprecate this model. Null for immediately deprecated models.|
|replacement_model|[LLM](#schemallm) \| null|false|none|The model that replaces this deprecated model. Traffic will be automatically routed to this model.|
|deprecation_config|[LLMDeprecationConfigModel](#schemallmdeprecationconfigmodel) \| null|false|none|Custom deprecation timing configuration for this model. Null if using the default configuration.|

```json
{
  "smb_tool_type": "list_customer_facing_agents"
}
```

List every customer-facing agent on the workspace.

The assistant uses this whenever it needs to act on a specific customer-facing
agent (rules, config edits, etc.) so it can pick the right ``agent_id`` to pass
to mutating tools. Mirrors the ``list_services`` / ``list_clients``
pattern: read once, then mutate by id.

<h2 id="tocS_LiteralJsonSchemaProperty">LiteralJsonSchemaProperty</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaliteraljsonschemaproperty"></a>
<a id="schema_LiteralJsonSchemaProperty"></a>
<a id="tocSliteraljsonschemaproperty"></a>
<a id="tocsliteraljsonschemaproperty"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "A user-provided message",
  "type": "string"
}
```

Schema property for literal JSON types. IMPORTANT: Only ONE of the following fields can be set: description (LLM provides value), dynamic_variable (value from variable), is_system_provided (system provides value), constant_value (fixed value), or is_omitted (parameter is omitted). These are mutually exclusive.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string \| [string]|true|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the property. When set, the LLM will provide the value based on this description. Mutually exclusive with dynamic_variable, is_system_provided, constant_value, and is_omitted.|
|enum|[string] \| null|false|none|List of allowed string values for string type parameters|
|is_system_provided|boolean|false|none|If true, the value will be populated by the system at runtime. Used by API Integration Webhook tools for templating. Mutually exclusive with description, dynamic_variable, constant_value, and is_omitted.|
|dynamic_variable|string|false|none|The name of the dynamic variable to use for this property's value. Mutually exclusive with description, is_system_provided, constant_value, and is_omitted.|
|allowed_values|[AllowedValues](#schemaallowedvalues) \| null|false|none|Server-side rejection guard for an LLM-provided value: the runtime rejects any value outside the permitted set this object names, and the set is not advertised to the LLM as an enum. Only supported when the value source is `description`; combining it with dynamic_variable, is_system_provided, constant_value, or is_omitted is rejected.|
|allowed_values_dynamic_variable|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED: use `allowed_values` instead. When set, the LLM provides the value but the runtime rejects any value not present in the list held by this dynamic variable (must be a JSON array such as ["ws_alpha", "ws_beta"]). Use to let the LLM pick from a server-verified set (e.g. the IDs the current user is allowed to access). Requires description; mutually exclusive with dynamic_variable, is_system_provided, constant_value, and is_omitted.|
|constant_value|string \| integer \| number \| boolean \| null|false|none|A constant value to use for this property. Mutually exclusive with description, dynamic_variable, is_system_provided, and is_omitted.|
|is_omitted|boolean|false|none|If true, this parameter will be completely omitted from the request. Only valid for optional parameters. Mutually exclusive with description, dynamic_variable, is_system_provided, and constant_value.|

|response_timeout_secs|integer|false|none|The maximum time in seconds to wait for each MCP tool call to complete. Must be between 5 and 300 seconds (inclusive).|
|tool_config_overrides|[[MCPToolConfigOverride-Input](#schemamcptoolconfigoverride-input)]|false|none|List of per-tool configuration overrides that override the server-level defaults for specific tools|
|disable_compression|boolean|false|none|Whether to disable HTTP compression for this MCP server. Enable this if the server does not support compressed responses.|

'allow' (default) lets the user interrupt at any time, 'disable_during_tool' suppresses interruptions only while the tool is running, 'disable_during_tool_and_turn' suppresses interruptions while the tool runs and for the agent response that follows it. Applies to every tool from this MCP server unless overridden per tool.|
|tool_call_sound|[ToolCallSoundType](#schematoolcallsoundtype) \| null|false|none|Predefined tool call sound type to play during tool execution for all tools from this MCP server|
|tool_call_sound_behavior|[ToolCallSoundBehavior](#schematoolcallsoundbehavior)|false|none|Determines when the tool call sound should play for all tools from this MCP server|
|execution_mode|[ToolExecutionMode](#schematoolexecutionmode)|false|none|Determines when and how all tools from this MCP server execute: 'immediate' executes the tool right away when requested by the LLM, 'post_tool_speech' waits for the agent to finish speaking before executing, 'async' runs the tool in the background without blocking - best for long-running operations.|
|response_timeout_secs|integer|false|none|The maximum time in seconds to wait for each MCP tool call to complete. Must be between 5 and 300 seconds (inclusive).|
|tool_config_overrides|[[MCPToolConfigOverride-Output](#schemamcptoolconfigoverride-output)]|false|none|List of per-tool configuration overrides that override the server-level defaults for specific tools|
|disable_compression|boolean|false|none|Whether to disable HTTP compression for this MCP server. Enable this if the server does not support compressed responses.|

An MCP tool configuration that can be used to call MCP servers

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|description|string|true|none|Description of when the tool should be used and what it does.|
|response_timeout_secs|integer|false|none|The maximum time in seconds to wait for the MCP tool call to complete. Must be between 5 and 300 seconds (inclusive).|
|disable_interruptions|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED: use `interruption_mode` instead. If true, the user will not be able to interrupt the agent while this tool is running.|
|interruption_mode|[ToolInterruptionMode](#schematoolinterruptionmode)|false|none|Controls whether the user can interrupt the agent around this tool call. 'allow' (default) lets the user interrupt at any time, 'disable_during_tool' suppresses interruptions only while the tool is running, 'disable_during_tool_and_turn' suppresses interruptions while the tool runs and for the agent response that follows it.|
|force_pre_tool_speech|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED: use `pre_tool_speech` instead. If true, the agent will speak before the tool call.|
|pre_tool_speech|[PreToolSpeechMode](#schemapretoolspeechmode)|false|none|Controls whether the agent speaks before this tool is called. 'auto' (default) decides based on recent tool latency, 'force' always asks the agent to speak, 'off' fully opts out regardless of latency.|
|assignments|[[DynamicVariableAssignment](#schemadynamicvariableassignment)]|false|none|Configuration for extracting values from tool responses and assigning them to dynamic variables|
|tool_call_sound|[ToolCallSoundType](#schematoolcallsoundtype) \| null|false|none|Predefined tool call sound type to play during tool execution. If not specified, no tool call sound will be played.|
|tool_call_sound_behavior|[ToolCallSoundBehavior](#schematoolcallsoundbehavior)|false|none|Determines when the tool call sound should play. 'auto' only plays when there's pre-tool speech, 'always' plays for every tool call.|
|tool_error_handling_mode|[ToolErrorHandlingMode](#schematoolerrorhandlingmode)|false|none|Controls how tool errors are processed before being shared with the agent. <h2 id="tocS_PricingMode">PricingMode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapricingmode"></a>
<a id="schema_PricingMode"></a>
<a id="tocSpricingmode"></a>
<a id="tocspricingmode"></a>

```json
"fixed"
```

Whether a catalog item's price and duration are known up front.

Orthogonal to :class:`SMBServiceKind`, which describes the *resource*
model (staff / asset / seats) rather than the price. A quotable service
can still be staff-delivered or asset-based, so this cannot be folded
into the kind discriminator.

- ``FIXED``: catalog price and duration apply (the default, and every
  pre-existing item).
- ``QUOTE``: neither is knowable until the owner has seen the job. The
  agent collects intake answers and files a quote request instead of
  booking a slot or taking an order.

<h2 id="tocS_PromptAgentAPIModel-Input">PromptAgentAPIModel-Input</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapromptagentapimodel-input"></a>
<a id="schema_PromptAgentAPIModel-Input"></a>
<a id="tocSpromptagentapimodel-input"></a>
<a id="tocspromptagentapimodel-input"></a>

```json
{
  "knowledge_base": [],
  "llm": "gemini-2.0-flash-001",
  "max_tokens": -1,
  "prompt": "You are a helpful assistant that can answer questions about the topic of the conversation.",
  "temperature": 0,
  "tool_ids": [],
  "tools": []
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|prompt|string|false|none|The prompt for the agent|
|llm|[LLM](#schemallm)|false|none|The LLM to query with the prompt and the chat history. If using data residency, the LLM must be supported in the data residency environment|
|reasoning_effort|[LLMReasoningEffort](#schemallmreasoningeffort) \| null|false|none|Reasoning effort of the model. Only available for some models.|
|service_tier|[LLMServiceTier](#schemallmservicetier)|false|none|Service tier of the model, trading a per-token price premium for higher token throughput. Only available for some models.|
|thinking_budget|integer \| null|false|none|Max number of tokens used for thinking. Use 0 to turn off if supported by the model.|
|enable_reasoning_summary|boolean|false|none|Enable model reasoning summaries. When disabled, we do not request summaries from provider if possible for faster TTFB. Not ZRM compatible.|
|temperature|number \| null|false|none|The temperature for the LLM. Defaults to 0. Set to null to omit the parameter from the LLM request entirely (useful for custom LLMs that reject the temperature field).|
|max_tokens|integer|false|none|If greater than 0, maximum number of tokens the LLM can predict|
|tool_ids|[string]|false|none|A list of IDs of tools used by the agent|
|tool_ids_strict|boolean|false|none|Only applies as a conversation override, allowed whenever tool_ids may be overridden. When true, the overridden tool_ids is the full list of tools allowed in the conversation, including tools on workflow nodes. Ignored when set on the agent.|
|built_in_tools|[BuiltInTools-Input](#schemabuiltintools-input)|false|none|Built-in system tools to be used by the agent|
|enable_parallel_tool_calls|boolean|false|none|Enable parallel tool calling. When enabled, the agent can execute multiple tools in parallel within a single turn. Not supported by all models.|
|mcp_server_ids|[string]|false|none|A list of MCP server ids to be used by the agent|
|native_mcp_server_ids|[string]|false|none|A list of Native MCP server ids to be used by the agent|
|knowledge_base|[[KnowledgeBaseLocator](#schemaknowledgebaselocator)]|false|none|A list of knowledge bases to be used by the agent|
|custom_llm|[CustomLLM](#schemacustomllm) \| null|false|none|Definition for a custom LLM if LLM field is set to 'CUSTOM_LLM'|
|ignore_default_personality|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to remove the default personality lines from the system prompt|
|rag|[RagConfig-Input](#schemaragconfig-input)|false|none|Configuration for RAG|
|timezone|string \| null|false|none|Timezone for displaying current time in system prompt. If set, the current time will be included in the system prompt using this timezone. Must be a valid timezone name (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'UTC'). Recommended for accurate time-aware responses; without this, the agent has no knowledge of the current date/time unless you provide it via dynamic variables or tools, which can lead to incorrect or hallucinated time references.|
|backup_llm_config|[BackupLLMDefault](#schemabackupllmdefault) \| [BackupLLMDisabled](#schemabackupllmdisabled) \| [BackupLLMOverride](#schemabackupllmoverride)|false|none|Configuration for backup LLM cascading. Can be disabled, use system defaults, or specify custom order.|
|cascade_timeout_seconds|number|false|none|Time in seconds before cascading to backup LLM. Must be between 2 and 15 seconds.|
|tools|[[WebhookToolConfig-Input](#schemawebhooktoolconfig-input) \| [ClientToolConfig-Input](#schemaclienttoolconfig-input) \| [SystemToolConfig-Input](#schemasystemtoolconfig-input) \| [MCPToolConfig-Input](#schemamcptoolconfig-input) \| [ApiIntegrationWebhookToolConfig-Input](#schemaapiintegrationwebhooktoolconfig-input) \| [SMBToolConfig](#schemasmbtoolconfig)]|false|none|**Deprecated.** A list of tools that the agent can use over the course of the conversation, use tool_ids instead|

<a id="schema_PromptAgentAPIModel-Output"></a>
<a id="tocSpromptagentapimodel-output"></a>
<a id="tocspromptagentapimodel-output"></a>

```json
{
  "knowledge_base": [],
  "llm": "gemini-2.0-flash-001",
  "max_tokens": -1,
  "prompt": "You are a helpful assistant that can answer questions about the topic of the conversation.",
  "temperature": 0,
  "tool_ids": [],
  "tools": []
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|prompt|string|false|none|The prompt for the agent|
|llm|[LLM](#schemallm)|false|none|The LLM to query with the prompt and the chat history. If using data residency, the LLM must be supported in the data residency environment|
|reasoning_effort|[LLMReasoningEffort](#schemallmreasoningeffort) \| null|false|none|Reasoning effort of the model. Only available for some models.|
|service_tier|[LLMServiceTier](#schemallmservicetier)|false|none|Service tier of the model, trading a per-token price premium for higher token throughput. Only available for some models.|
|thinking_budget|integer \| null|false|none|Max number of tokens used for thinking. Use 0 to turn off if supported by the model.|
|enable_reasoning_summary|boolean|false|none|Enable model reasoning summaries. When disabled, we do not request summaries from provider if possible for faster TTFB. Not ZRM compatible.|
|temperature|number \| null|false|none|The temperature for the LLM. Defaults to 0. Set to null to omit the parameter from the LLM request entirely (useful for custom LLMs that reject the temperature field).|
|max_tokens|integer|false|none|If greater than 0, maximum number of tokens the LLM can predict|
|tool_ids|[string]|false|none|A list of IDs of tools used by the agent|
|tool_ids_strict|boolean|false|none|Only applies as a conversation override, allowed whenever tool_ids may be overridden. When true, the overridden tool_ids is the full list of tools allowed in the conversation, including tools on workflow nodes. Ignored when set on the agent.|
|built_in_tools|[BuiltInTools-Output](#schemabuiltintools-output)|false|none|Built-in system tools to be used by the agent|
|enable_parallel_tool_calls|boolean|false|none|Enable parallel tool calling. When enabled, the agent can execute multiple tools in parallel within a single turn. Not supported by all models.|
|mcp_server_ids|[string]|false|none|A list of MCP server ids to be used by the agent|
|native_mcp_server_ids|[string]|false|none|A list of Native MCP server ids to be used by the agent|
|knowledge_base|[[KnowledgeBaseLocator](#schemaknowledgebaselocator)]|false|none|A list of knowledge bases to be used by the agent|
|custom_llm|[CustomLLM](#schemacustomllm) \| null|false|none|Definition for a custom LLM if LLM field is set to 'CUSTOM_LLM'|
|ignore_default_personality|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to remove the default personality lines from the system prompt|
|rag|[RagConfig-Output](#schemaragconfig-output)|false|none|Configuration for RAG|
|timezone|string \| null|false|none|Timezone for displaying current time in system prompt. If set, the current time will be included in the system prompt using this timezone. Must be a valid timezone name (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'UTC'). Recommended for accurate time-aware responses; without this, the agent has no knowledge of the current date/time unless you provide it via dynamic variables or tools, which can lead to incorrect or hallucinated time references.|
|backup_llm_config|[BackupLLMDefault](#schemabackupllmdefault) \| [BackupLLMDisabled](#schemabackupllmdisabled) \| [BackupLLMOverride](#schemabackupllmoverride)|false|none|Configuration for backup LLM cascading. Can be disabled, use system defaults, or specify custom order.|
|cascade_timeout_seconds|number|false|none|Time in seconds before cascading to backup LLM. Must be between 2 and 15 seconds.|
|tools|[[WebhookToolConfig-Output](#schemawebhooktoolconfig-output) \| [ClientToolConfig-Output](#schemaclienttoolconfig-output) \| [SystemToolConfig-Output](#schemasystemtoolconfig-output) \| [MCPToolConfig-Output](#schemamcptoolconfig-output) \| [ApiIntegrationWebhookToolConfig-Output](#schemaapiintegrationwebhooktoolconfig-output) \| [SMBToolConfig](#schemasmbtoolconfig)]|false|none|**Deprecated.** A list of tools that the agent can use over the course of the conversation, use tool_ids instead|

|cascade_timeout_seconds|number \| null|false|none|Time in seconds before cascading to backup LLM. Must be between 2 and 15 seconds.|
|tools|[[WebhookToolConfig-Output](#schemawebhooktoolconfig-output) \| [ClientToolConfig-Output](#schemaclienttoolconfig-output) \| [SystemToolConfig-Output](#schemasystemtoolconfig-output) \| [MCPToolConfig-Output](#schemamcptoolconfig-output) \| [ApiIntegrationWebhookToolConfig-Output](#schemaapiintegrationwebhooktoolconfig-output) \| [SMBToolConfig](#schemasmbtoolconfig)] \| null|false|none|A list of tools that the agent can use over the course of the conversation, use tool_ids instead|

```json
{
  "conversation_goal_prompt": "Determine whether the agent fully resolved the user's issue.",
  "id": "criterion_binary_001",
  "max_score": 100,
  "name": "Issue resolved",
  "scope": "conversation",
  "scoring_mode": "binary",
  "use_knowledge_base": false
}
```

An evaluation using the transcript and a prompt for a yes/no achieved answer

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier for the evaluation criteria|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|type|string|false|none|The type of evaluation criteria|
|conversation_goal_prompt|string|true|none|The prompt that the agent should use to evaluate the conversation|
|use_knowledge_base|boolean|false|none|When evaluating the prompt, should the agent's knowledge base be used.|
|scope|[AnalysisScope](#schemaanalysisscope)|false|none|The scope of transcript context used when evaluating this criterion. 'conversation' uses the full transcript; 'agent' uses only the portion where the defining agent was active.|
|llm|[LLM](#schemallm) \| null|false|none|LLM model to use for this evaluation criteria. If not set, uses agent's analysis_llm default.|
|scoring_mode|[CriteriaScoringMode](#schemacriteriascoringmode)|false|none|How this criterion is scored. 'binary' resolves to success/failure/unknown. 'numeric_uniform' returns a number on the [0, max_score] scale which is normalized into the aggregate conversation success percentage.|
|max_score|integer|false|none|Maximum value of the numeric score scale (minimum is always 0). Only used when scoring_mode is 'numeric_uniform'.|
|score_instructions|string \| null|false|none|Optional free-text instructions describing how to assign values on the numeric scale. Only used when scoring_mode is 'numeric_uniform'.|

|Property|Value|

|scope|agent|

<h2 id="tocS_ResellerWorkspaceSubscription">ResellerWorkspaceSubscription</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresellerworkspacesubscription"></a>
<a id="schema_ResellerWorkspaceSubscription"></a>
<a id="tocSresellerworkspacesubscription"></a>
<a id="tocsresellerworkspacesubscription"></a>

```json
{
  "tier_id": "string",
  "billing_period": "monthly_period",
  "billing_period_end_unix": 0,
  "cancel_at_unix": 0,
  "pending_downgrade_tier": "string",
  "pending_downgrade_at_unix": 0
}
```

A reseller-managed paid subscription, as the reseller can act on it.

Present only for a workspace the reseller actually sells to: untiered and
trial workspaces have no subscription to change or end, and are assigned to
instead. Projected from ``SMBBillingState`` rather than read from Stripe,
so it is the same state the grant path wrote.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tier_id|string|true|none|none|
|billing_period|string \| null|true|none|Cadence being billed. None only for a subscription mid-provisioning.|
|billing_period_end_unix|integer|true|none|When the current period ends, and so when a deferred change lands.|
|cancel_at_unix|integer \| null|false|none|When Stripe will end the subscription. Set means a pending unassignment the reseller can still undo.|
|pending_downgrade_tier|string \| null|false|none|Tier this workspace drops to at the period boundary, if a downgrade is already scheduled.|
|pending_downgrade_at_unix|integer \| null|false|none|When that scheduled downgrade takes effect.|

|resource_type|[WorkspaceResourceType](#schemaworkspaceresourcetype)|true|none|The type of the resource.|
|creator_user_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the user who created the resource.|
|anonymous_access_level_override|string \| null|true|none|The access level for anonymous users. If None, the resource is not shared publicly.|
|role_to_group_ids|object|true|none|A mapping of grant slots to group IDs. Keys are the preset access roles plus workspace custom-role ids ('role_...'). When the resource is shared with a user, the group id is the user's id.|
|share_options|[[ShareOptionResponseModel](#schemashareoptionresponsemodel)]|true|none|List of options for sharing the resource further in the workspace. These are users who don't have access to the resource yet.|

<h2 id="tocS_ResponseFilter">ResponseFilter</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresponsefilter"></a>
<a id="schema_ResponseFilter"></a>
<a id="tocSresponsefilter"></a>
<a id="tocsresponsefilter"></a>

```json
{
  "mode": "all",
  "filters": [
    "string"
  ],
  "content_type": "application/json"
}
```

Configuration for filtering tool responses before they are visible to the agent.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|[ResponseFilterMode](#schemaresponsefiltermode)|false|none|Controls how tool responses are filtered. 'all' returns entire response, 'allow' returns only specified paths, 'hide_all' hides the entire response.|
|filters|[string]|false|none|Dot notation paths to include when mode is 'allow' (e.g., ['ticket.id', 'ticket.status']).|
|content_type|string|false|none|Content type for response filtering. Only 'application/json' responses are filtered.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|all|
|mode|allow|
|mode|hide_all|

<h2 id="tocS_SMBAddOn">SMBAddOn</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasmbaddon"></a>
<a id="schema_SMBAddOn"></a>
<a id="tocSsmbaddon"></a>
<a id="tocssmbaddon"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "add_duration_minutes": 0,
  "add_price": 0
}
```

A standalone add-on that can be tacked onto a service or rental booking.

An add-on is a small, free-form extra (e.g. "Hot towel", "Valet parking")
that extends the parent booking's duration and total price without
creating a separate calendar event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Stable identifier used by booking requests and calendar snapshots. Survives name/price edits, so rebooking and reporting stay consistent.|
|name|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|true|none|none|
|description|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|false|none|Short owner-authored blurb shown to customers and voice agents when they're choosing add-ons. Empty string means no description.|
|add_duration_minutes|integer|false|none|Minutes added to the parent booking when this add-on is selected.|
|add_price|number|false|none|Amount added to the parent booking's total when this add-on is selected.|

```json
    }
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pricing_mode|[PricingMode](#schemapricingmode)|false|none|'fixed' (default): the item has a known price the agent can quote, and customers can book or order it directly. 'quote': the price depends on the job (renovation, catering, custom work), so no price or slot is offered; the agent collects the intake_questions and files a quote request instead. Takes effect only while quotes are enabled for the business. Group services cannot use 'quote'.|
|intake_questions|[[SMBIntakeQuestion](#schemasmbintakequestion)]|false|none|Questions the agent asks before booking or ordering this item. Required for a useful ``pricing_mode='quote'`` item -- without them a quote request arrives with nothing to price -- but also valid on fixed-price items that need extra detail (current hair color before a dye job, allergies before a treatment).|
|groups|[[SMBGroupMembership](#schemasmbgroupmembership)]|false|none|Group memberships for this item. Each entry carries the group label and the item's 0-based rank within that group.|
|ungrouped_rank|integer \| null|false|none|Display position among items with no group; `null` sorts last. Change it with the reorder endpoint.|
|name|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|true|none|none|
|description|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|false|none|none|
|variants|[[SMBServiceVariant](#schemasmbservicevariant)]|false|none|Bookable options for this service. Always non-empty; ``variants[0]`` is the default option shown when callers don't pick a specific variant. Each entry has its own duration and (optional) price, and uniqueness is keyed by duration.|
|kind|[SMBServiceKind](#schemasmbservicekind)|false|none|Classic = staff-delivered; rental = asset-based; group = multi-participant session. Populated by the extraction category.|
|buffer_minutes|integer|false|none|Turnover/cleanup time reserved after each booking. Applies to every service kind; default 0 means no buffer.|
|service_location|[ServiceLocationType](#schemaservicelocationtype)|false|none|Where the service is delivered. ``business`` = client visits the business location (default); ``customer`` = staff travels to the client. Only meaningful for ``kind='classic'``.|
|add_ons|[[SMBAddOn](#schemasmbaddon)]|false|none|Optional extras scraped from the website that can be attached to a booking of this service.|
|max_participants|integer \| null|false|none|Capacity for ``kind='group'``: how many seats a single session can sell across all registrations. Must be ``None`` for classic and rental services (those are always exclusive to one client per booking).|
|capacity|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|is_active|boolean|false|none|none|
|any_staff_member|boolean|false|none|none|
|staff_ids|[string]|false|none|Staff assigned to this service; must be empty for kind='rental'.|
|asset_ids|[string]|false|none|none|
|advance_booking_minutes|integer|false|none|How far into the future customer-facing channels (public booking page, voice agent) may book this service. Applies to every kind.|
|location_ids|[string]|false|none|Locations where this service is offered; empty list means all locations.|
|display_on_booking_page|boolean|false|none|none|
|travel_minutes|integer|false|none|Travel time in minutes added before/after appointments for customer-location services. Blocks the staff member's calendar but is not visible to the customer. Ignored when ``service_location='business'``.|
|travel_before|boolean|false|none|Add travel time before the appointment (outbound trip).|
|travel_after|boolean|false|none|Add travel time after the appointment (return trip).|
|promotions|[[SMBServicePromotion](#schemasmbservicepromotion)]|false|none|Time-bound discounts applicable to this service or specific variants.|

|pricing_mode|quote|
|kind|classic|
|kind|rental|
|kind|group|
|service_location|business|
|service_location|customer|

Membership of an item in a single user-defined group, with its display
rank inside that group.

`rank` is the 0-based position the item occupies within the group's
section in the dashboard. Items default to rank 0 when added to a group
and are rewritten by the dedicated reorder endpoints.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|label|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|true|none|none|
|rank|integer|false|none|0-based display position within this group in the dashboard. Change it with the reorder endpoint; send back the value you read to keep the order, a membership sent without it goes to position 0.|

<h2 id="tocS_SMBIntakeQuestion">SMBIntakeQuestion</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasmbintakequestion"></a>
<a id="schema_SMBIntakeQuestion"></a>
<a id="tocSsmbintakequestion"></a>
<a id="tocssmbintakequestion"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "kind": "text",
  "options": [
    "string"
  ],
  "required": false,
  "is_active": true
}
```

One owner-authored question the agent asks before booking/ordering this item.

This is the structured counterpart to the agent-wide
``CustomerFacingConfig.details_to_collect``: scoped to a single catalog
item, and typed so the answer is usable afterwards (rendered in the inbox,
filterable, and eventually an input to pricing) rather than just readable.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Stable identifier referenced by stored answers. Survives label edits so history stays attributable to the right question.|
|label|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|true|none|The question as the agent should ask it, e.g. 'How many rooms?'. Phrased by the owner; the agent may rephrase for conversational flow but must not change what is being asked.|
|kind|[IntakeQuestionKind](#schemaintakequestionkind)|false|none|Answer shape for a per-item intake question.|
|options|[[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)]|false|none|Allowed answers for ``kind='choice'``. Must be empty for the other kinds.|
|required|boolean|false|none|On the public booking page this is enforced as a form constraint. On a voice call it is only an instruction to the agent: hard-rejecting a booking mid-conversation because the caller dodged a question is worse for the caller than a booking with a gap the owner can chase. Do not 'fix' this into a server-side constraint for the voice path.|
|is_active|boolean|false|none|Retired questions are deactivated rather than deleted, so answers already stored against them keep resolving.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|text|
|kind|number|
|kind|choice|

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|phone_number|[PhoneNumber](#schemaphonenumber) \| null|false|none|Phone number in E.164 format (for indexing/filtering)|
|is_byo|boolean|false|none|True when the phone is bring-your-own: registered by the workspace using their own telephony provider (Twilio credentials or SIP trunk). BYO phones are never part of the shared pool, do not count against the tier-based phone quota, and are deleted (rather than returned to the pool) on release.|
|provider|string|false|none|Telephony provider for this phone number. Defaults to twilio for backwards compatibility with existing documents.|
|nanp_area_code|integer|false|none|US/Canada NANP area code (NPA) as an integer.|
|customer_facing_agent_id|string \| null|false|none|Determines assignment status: None = pool (unassigned), non-None = assigned to this customer-facing agent. When set, inbound calls to this phone route to that agent.|
|deactivated_at_unix|integer \| null|false|none|Unix timestamp when this assignment was deactivated. Drives the per-assignment 14-day grace cleanup. None when active.|
|deactivation_reason|[SMBPhoneAssignmentDeactivationReason](#schemasmbphoneassignmentdeactivationreason) \| null|false|none|Why this assignment was deactivated. None when active.|
|regulatory_status|[SMBPhoneRegulatoryStatus](#schemasmbphoneregulatorystatus) \| null|false|none|None for numbers from countries with no regulatory requirements. 'held' while the workspace's own application is under review, 'approved' once it passed and the number is fully usable.|
|regulatory_number_type|[ApplicationNumberType](#schemaapplicationnumbertype) \| null|false|none|Which regulated type this number was issued as. Set on numbers bought in a country that needs paperwork, so the request form can open on the type the workspace already holds. None for pool numbers, which need no application.|
|regulatory_country|[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode) \| null|false|none|ISO country the regulated number was bought in. Recorded so a held number can be matched to the application it belongs to without inferring the country from the dialing prefix. None for pool numbers.|
|_id|string|true|none|none|
|created_at_unix|[UnixTimestamp](#schemaunixtimestamp)|false|none|Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)|
|updated_at_unix|[UnixTimestamp](#schemaunixtimestamp)|false|none|Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)|

Regulatory standing of a number in a country that requires paperwork.

Absent (``None``) on numbers from countries with no requirements, which is
every pooled US/Canada number — those are usable the moment they are bought.

<h2 id="tocS_SMBProcedure">SMBProcedure</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasmbprocedure"></a>
<a id="schema_SMBProcedure"></a>
<a id="tocSsmbprocedure"></a>
<a id="tocssmbprocedure"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "trigger": "string",
  "body": "",
  "id": "string",
  "created_at_unix": 0,
  "source_key": "string"
}
```

A standard operating procedure (SOP) the receptionist can run on calls.

Like :class:`AgentRule`, this is user-owned config that lives on the agent's
:class:`CustomerFacingConfig` in agent-info. It is materialized into the
agents-cluster procedure store lazily, on the next agent rebuild. ``id`` is
the stable convai ``procedure_id`` so it survives rebuilds and version bumps.

``body`` becomes the procedure's content.

``source_key`` is set when the procedure was copied from an integration.
It is ``{provider_id}-{template_key}`` and is never translated, so the
settings UI can tell the copy from one the owner wrote after the name,
trigger, and steps have been localized.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|true|none|Name of the procedure.|
|trigger|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|true|none|When the receptionist should run the procedure, in natural language. The receptionist matches caller requests against it, e.g. 'When the caller wants to book an appointment'.|
|body|string|false|none|Step-by-step instructions, as markdown.|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|created_at_unix|[UnixTimestamp](#schemaunixtimestamp)|false|none|Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)|
|source_key|string \| null|false|none|none|

<a id="tocssmbtransferrule"></a>

```json
{
  "label": "string",
  "phone_number": "string",
  "condition": "string",
  "post_dial_digits": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "created_at_unix": 0
}
```

A configured phone number that the agent can transfer calls to.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|label|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|true|none|Name of the transfer destination, e.g. 'Alvin' or 'Billing team'.|
|phone_number|[PhoneNumber](#schemaphonenumber)|true|none|Number to transfer to. Without a country code it is dialed locally in the business's country, so include the country code for a number abroad.|
|condition|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|true|none|What the caller does that triggers the transfer, e.g. 'The caller asks to speak to a human or to Alvin'. Describe only the trigger; do not restate the phone number or the word 'transfer'.|
|post_dial_digits|string \| null|false|none|DTMF digits automatically played after the transfer destination picks up (e.g. '1' to answer a 'press 1 to accept' screen, or 'www1234' to key an extension after a pause). Valid characters are 0-9, *, #, w (0.5s pause) and W (1s pause). Twilio transfers only.|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|created_at_unix|[UnixTimestamp](#schemaunixtimestamp)|false|none|Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)|

```json
  ],

    {
```
```json
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",

      "promotional_price": 0,
      "days_of_week": [
        0
      ],

    }
  ],

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pricing_mode|[PricingMode](#schemapricingmode)|false|none|'fixed' (default): the item has a known price the agent can quote, and customers can book or order it directly. 'quote': the price depends on the job (renovation, catering, custom work), so no price or slot is offered; the agent collects the intake_questions and files a quote request instead. Takes effect only while quotes are enabled for the business. Group services cannot use 'quote'.|
|intake_questions|[[SMBIntakeQuestion](#schemasmbintakequestion)]|false|none|Questions the agent asks before booking or ordering this item. Required for a useful ``pricing_mode='quote'`` item -- without them a quote request arrives with nothing to price -- but also valid on fixed-price items that need extra detail (current hair color before a dye job, allergies before a treatment).|
|groups|[[SMBGroupMembership](#schemasmbgroupmembership)]|false|none|Group memberships for this item. Each entry carries the group label and the item's 0-based rank within that group.|
|ungrouped_rank|integer \| null|false|none|Display position among items with no group; `null` sorts last. Change it with the reorder endpoint.|
|name|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|false|none|none|
|description|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|false|none|none|
|variants|[[SMBServiceVariant](#schemasmbservicevariant)]|false|none|Bookable options for this service. Always non-empty; ``variants[0]`` is the default option shown when callers don't pick a specific variant. Each entry has its own duration and (optional) price, and uniqueness is keyed by duration.|
|kind|[SMBServiceKind](#schemasmbservicekind)|false|none|Classic = staff-delivered; rental = asset-based; group = multi-participant session. Populated by the extraction category.|
|buffer_minutes|integer|false|none|Turnover/cleanup time reserved after each booking. Applies to every service kind; default 0 means no buffer.|
|service_location|[ServiceLocationType](#schemaservicelocationtype)|false|none|Where the service is delivered. ``business`` = client visits the business location (default); ``customer`` = staff travels to the client. Only meaningful for ``kind='classic'``.|
|add_ons|[[SMBAddOn](#schemasmbaddon)]|false|none|Optional extras scraped from the website that can be attached to a booking of this service.|
|max_participants|integer \| null|false|none|Capacity for ``kind='group'``: how many seats a single session can sell across all registrations. Must be ``None`` for classic and rental services (those are always exclusive to one client per booking).|
|capacity|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|is_active|boolean|false|none|none|
|any_staff_member|boolean|false|none|none|
|staff_ids|[string]|false|none|Staff assigned to this service; must be empty for kind='rental'.|
|asset_ids|[string]|false|none|none|
|advance_booking_minutes|integer|false|none|How far into the future customer-facing channels (public booking page, voice agent) may book this service. Applies to every kind.|
|location_ids|[string]|false|none|Locations where this service is offered; empty list means all locations.|
|display_on_booking_page|boolean|false|none|none|
|travel_minutes|integer|false|none|Travel time in minutes added before/after appointments for customer-location services. Blocks the staff member's calendar but is not visible to the customer. Ignored when ``service_location='business'``.|
|travel_before|boolean|false|none|Add travel time before the appointment (outbound trip).|
|travel_after|boolean|false|none|Add travel time after the appointment (return trip).|
|promotions|[[SMBServicePromotion](#schemasmbservicepromotion)]|false|none|Time-bound discounts applicable to this service or specific variants.|
|duration_minutes|integer \| null|false|none|Sets the first variant's duration. Ignored when `variants` is sent.|
|price|number \| null|false|none|Sets the first variant's price. Ignored when `variants` is sent.|

|pricing_mode|fixed|
|pricing_mode|quote|
|kind|classic|
|kind|rental|
|kind|group|
|service_location|business|
|service_location|customer|

|photo_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|none|
|location_id|string \| null|false|none|Location this staff member is assigned to; empty means available at all locations.|
|working_hours|[WorkingHours](#schemaworkinghours) \| null|false|none|Custom working hours for this staff member. None means follow the assigned location's operating_hours (requires location_id).|
|display_on_booking_page|boolean|false|none|Whether customers can see and pick this staff member by name on the booking page. False keeps them bookable, just not shown by name.|
|customer_facing_name|[StrippedStr](#schemastrippedstr)|false|none|Optional public-facing label. When empty, `name` is shown to customers too. `name` stays the internal/admin label used in the dashboard and business-owner notifications.|

<h2 id="tocS_SMBWidgetAppearance">SMBWidgetAppearance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasmbwidgetappearance"></a>
<a id="schema_SMBWidgetAppearance"></a>
<a id="tocSsmbwidgetappearance"></a>
<a id="tocssmbwidgetappearance"></a>

```json
{
  "orb_color_1": "string",
  "orb_color_2": "string",
  "variant": "tiny",
  "placement": "top-left",
  "dismissible": true,
  "main_label": "string",
  "start_call": "string"
}
```

How the website widget looks -- the only part of its config SMB exposes.

Unlike the rest of a receptionist's settings this is not SMB data: it is
written straight onto the ConvAI agent's ``platform_settings.widget``. The
value types mirror ConvAI's ``WidgetConfig`` by hand because
``xi_reception`` must not depend on ``xi_agents``; they are the widget's
public API, so they are stable.

A ``None`` label means "no override", which keeps the widget following the
agent's language instead of freezing today's translation into the config.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|orb_color_1|string|true|none|none|
|orb_color_2|string|true|none|none|
|variant|string|true|none|none|
|placement|string|true|none|none|
|dismissible|boolean|true|none|none|
|main_label|string \| null|false|none|none|
|start_call|string \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|variant|tiny|
|variant|compact|
|variant|full|
|placement|top-left|
|placement|top|
|placement|top-right|
|placement|bottom-left|
|placement|bottom|
|placement|bottom-right|

<h2 id="tocS_SkipTurnToolConfig">SkipTurnToolConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaskipturntoolconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_SkipTurnToolConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSskipturntoolconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsskipturntoolconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "system_tool_type": "skip_turn",
  "wait_timeout_secs": -1
}
```

Allows the agent to explicitly skip its turn.

This tool should be invoked by the LLM when the user indicates they would like
to think or take a short pause before continuing the conversation—e.g. when
they say: "Give me a second", "Let me think", or "One moment please".  After
calling this tool, the assistant should not speak until the user speaks
again, or if wait_timeout_secs is set, until that wait elapses and the
agent generates a check-in.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|system_tool_type|string|false|none|none|
|wait_timeout_secs|number|false|none|Seconds to wait after skip_turn before the agent generates a contextual check-in. The "End conversation after silence" timer is paused during the wait. -1 disables the wait: after skip_turn the agent stays silent until the caller speaks, and that timer keeps running. Applies to voice conversations only.|

<a id="tocSsmbsiptransport"></a>
<a id="tocssmbsiptransport"></a>

```json
"udp"
```

Signalling transport for outbound SIP INVITEs.

Values match the Agents platform ``SIPTrunkTransportEnum`` so the SMB adapter
maps by value. ``AUTO`` is omitted: the Agents UI hides it too, since it can
pick UDP, which is known to misbehave (CAI-299). Reception defaults to TLS.

<h2 id="tocS_SoftTimeoutConfig">SoftTimeoutConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasofttimeoutconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_SoftTimeoutConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSsofttimeoutconfig"></a>
<a id="tocssofttimeoutconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "message": "Hhmmmm...yeah.",
  "timeout_seconds": 2,
  "use_llm_generated_message": false
}
```

Configuration for soft timeout functionality during LLM response generation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|timeout_seconds|number|false|none|Time in seconds before showing the predefined message while waiting for LLM response. Set to -1 to disable.|
|message|string|false|none|Message to show when the first soft timeout is reached while waiting for LLM response. Supports dynamic variables (e.g., {{system__time}}, {{custom_variable}}).|
|additional_soft_timeout_messages|[string]|false|none|Extra static filler messages for subsequent soft timeouts in the same LLM generation. The first timeout uses `message`. If fewer messages are configured than `max_soft_timeouts_per_generation`, the last configured message is repeated; otherwise a built-in filler is used.|
|use_llm_generated_message|boolean|false|none|If enabled, the soft timeout message will be generated dynamically instead of using the static message.|
|randomize_fillers|boolean|false|none|If enabled, shuffle the order of static soft timeout messages once at the start of each turn. Only applies when use_llm_generated_message is false.|
|max_soft_timeouts_per_generation|integer|false|none|Maximum filler messages while waiting for a single LLM response. Fires every timeout_seconds until the LLM streams content or this limit is reached.|
|llm_generated_message_prompt_override|string \| null|false|none|Custom prompt for generating the soft timeout filler message when use_llm_generated_message is enabled. Recent conversation context is provided as a separate user message. If not set, the default prompt will be used. Supports dynamic variables (e.g., {{system__time}}, {{custom_variable}}).|
|disable_until_first_user_message|boolean|false|none|When true, soft timeout fillers are suppressed until the conversation has at least one real user message. Prevents fillers during the agent's opening turn (e.g. workflow generate-immediately / tool calls before the user speaks).|

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of tool|
|name|string|true|none|none|

|response_timeout_secs|integer|false|none|The maximum time in seconds to wait for the tool call to complete.|
|disable_interruptions|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED: use `interruption_mode` instead. If true, the user will not be able to interrupt the agent while this tool is running.|
|interruption_mode|[ToolInterruptionMode](#schematoolinterruptionmode)|false|none|Controls whether the user can interrupt the agent around this tool call. 'allow' (default) lets the user interrupt at any time, 'disable_during_tool' suppresses interruptions only while the tool is running, 'disable_during_tool_and_turn' suppresses interruptions while the tool runs and for the agent response that follows it.|
|force_pre_tool_speech|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED: use `pre_tool_speech` instead. If true, the agent will speak before the tool call.|
|pre_tool_speech|[PreToolSpeechMode](#schemapretoolspeechmode)|false|none|Controls whether the agent speaks before this tool is called. 'auto' (default) decides based on recent tool latency, 'force' always asks the agent to speak, 'off' fully opts out regardless of latency.|
|assignments|[[DynamicVariableAssignment](#schemadynamicvariableassignment)]|false|none|Configuration for extracting values from tool responses and assigning them to dynamic variables|
|tool_call_sound|[ToolCallSoundType](#schematoolcallsoundtype) \| null|false|none|Predefined tool call sound type to play during tool execution. If not specified, no tool call sound will be played.|
|tool_call_sound_behavior|[ToolCallSoundBehavior](#schematoolcallsoundbehavior)|false|none|Determines when the tool call sound should play. 'auto' only plays when there's pre-tool speech, 'always' plays for every tool call.|
|tool_error_handling_mode|[ToolErrorHandlingMode](#schematoolerrorhandlingmode)|false|none|Controls how tool errors are processed before being shared with the agent. 'auto' determines handling based on tool type (summarized for native integrations, hide for others), 'summarized' sends an LLM-generated summary, 'passthrough' sends the raw error, 'hide' does not share the error with the agent.|
|params|[EndCallToolConfig](#schemaendcalltoolconfig) \| [LanguageDetectionToolConfig](#schemalanguagedetectiontoolconfig) \| [TransferToAgentToolConfig-Input](#schematransfertoagenttoolconfig-input) \| [TransferToNumberToolConfig-Input](#schematransfertonumbertoolconfig-input) \| [SkipTurnToolConfig](#schemaskipturntoolconfig) \| [PlayDTMFToolConfig](#schemaplaydtmftoolconfig) \| [VoicemailDetectionToolConfig](#schemavoicemaildetectiontoolconfig) \| [KnowledgeBaseRagToolConfig](#schemaknowledgebaseragtoolconfig) \| [KnowledgeBaseToolConfig](#schemaknowledgebasetoolconfig) \| [StartProcedureToolConfig](#schemastartproceduretoolconfig) \| [EndProcedureToolConfig](#schemaendproceduretoolconfig)|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_TelephonyCallConfig-Input">TelephonyCallConfig-Input</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematelephonycallconfig-input"></a>
<a id="schema_TelephonyCallConfig-Input"></a>
<a id="tocStelephonycallconfig-input"></a>
<a id="tocstelephonycallconfig-input"></a>

```json
{
  "ringing_timeout_secs": 60,
  "twilio_call_recording_enabled": false,
  "twilio_machine_detection": {
    "mode": "enable",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "hang_up",
        "answered_by": [
          "human"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ringing_timeout_secs|integer|false|none|How long to ring the recipient before giving up, in seconds. Note that this will also be limited by the provider's own constraints.|
|twilio_call_recording_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to record the call using Twilio call recording. Ignored for non-Twilio providers. Recordings are stored in your Twilio account.|
|twilio_machine_detection|[TwilioMachineDetectionConfig](#schematwiliomachinedetectionconfig) \| null|false|none|Configuration for Twilio's carrier-level answering machine detection (AMD). Omit or set to null to disable it. Ignored for non-Twilio providers and for inbound calls. The resulting verdict is delivered as its own `answering_machine_detection` webhook event, which requires that event to be enabled on the workspace or agent webhook settings; it is not part of the conversation or the post-call webhook. Detection runs asynchronously so it never delays the start of the conversation, and the verdict can arrive at any point during the call -- with `detect_message_end`, even after it has ended. Twilio bills separately for AMD.|

element, each an output in its own right with its own `status`. A list can
be arbitrarily long, so `content` is its first page; when `has_more` is

Present only when `status` is `completed`. When `has_more` is true this is not the whole list. Reserved: no template produces this kind of output yet; it is published so that templates which do can be run with the same client.|

```json
{
  "id": "prompt",

    "title": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "enum": [
      "string"
    ]
  }

```

One input or output port of a published template version.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The port id. Input ids are the keys of the `inputs` map on `POST /v1/flows/templates/{template_id}/runs`; output ids are the keys of the `outputs` map on the run response.|
|content_schema|[ContentSchema](#schemacontentschema)|true|none|What this port accepts or produces, as a `ContentSchema`. Its `title` is the port's display name and its `description` is the help text the template author wrote. For an input, its `type` decides what value is accepted: `string` takes a bare string or a `generation` reference, `voice` takes a `voice` reference, and `image`/`video`/`audio` take an `asset`, `generation` or `inline_base64` reference. `number`, `integer` and `boolean` take a JSON value of that type. An `array` input takes a JSON array with one value per element, each admissible for its `items`. `object` inputs cannot be bound through this API yet. A `string` schema may carry an `enum` of the only values accepted. For an output, its `type` decides which `Template<Kind>Output` shape the run response holds under the port id.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inputs|object|true|none|Input values keyed by input port id. Every input port of the version being run must be given; a missing or unknown id is rejected. Pass `{}` for a template with no inputs.|
|version_id|string \| null|false|none|The template snapshot to run. Pass a specific version id to pin that snapshot, or `latest` (the default when omitted) to run the template's most recently published version. Only published versions can be pinned, except by the template's owner, who may also pin an unpublished saved snapshot to try it out before publishing. The live draft is never run through this API.|
|webhook|[WebhookTarget](#schemawebhooktarget) \| null|false|none|Include to send the run's result to the workspace's configured flows webhooks once the run's `status` reaches `completed` or `failed`. One event for the whole run: the `flows_template_run` event's `data` matches the terminal response of `GET /v1/flows/templates/{template_id}/runs/{run_id}`.|

```json
"string"
```

One value bound to a template input port, in the form its `content_schema`
calls for. A `string` port takes the text itself; `number`, `integer` and
`boolean` ports take a JSON value of that type. Anything stored elsewhere is
a reference discriminated on `type`: a prior `generation`, an uploaded
`asset`, a `voice`, or media passed `inline_base64`. An `array` port takes a
JSON array with one value per element, admissible for the schema's `items`.
`object` ports cannot be bound through this API yet.

No constraints beyond the wire shape live here: what a port accepts (an
`enum`, a length) is stated by its `content_schema`, and the run path
validates against that same schema.

|*anyOf*|string|false|none|none|

|*anyOf*|integer|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|number|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[TemplateInputReference](#schematemplateinputreference)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[[TemplateRunInput](#schematemplateruninput)]|false|none|none|

```json
    "product_demo": {
      "id": "QWr5N6X9ZTqf8jD2La3B",
      "status": "generating",
      "type": "video"
    },
    "product_still": {
      "content_mime_type": "image/png",
      "content_url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/generations/JWr5N6X9ZTqf8jD2LmQb",
      "id": "JWr5N6X9ZTqf8jD2LmQb",
      "status": "completed",
      "type": "image"
    }
  },
  "status": "generating",
  "template_id": "tmpl_abc123",
  "version_id": "ver_01hxyz"
}
```

A template run and its outputs. Every output exists from the moment the
run is created and reports its own `status`; the run's `status` rolls them
up, and the run is finished once it is `completed` or `failed`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the run.|
|template_id|string|true|none|The template this run executed, so a webhook consumer running several templates can tell their runs apart without keeping a run-to-template map.|
|version_id|string|true|none|The template version this run executed. Resolved when the run is created, so a run started with `latest` records the concrete version it ran.|
|status|[TemplateRunStatus](#schematemplaterunstatus)|true|none|The run's status, rolled up from its outputs: `pending` until an output starts, `generating` while any output is unfinished, `completed` once every output has completed, and `failed` once every output has finished and at least one failed. `completed` and `failed` are terminal: the `flows_template_run` webhook fires once the run reaches either.|
|outputs|object|true|none|The run's outputs, keyed by output port id. Each is a `TemplateOutput` discriminated on `type`, the `type` of its port's `content_schema`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|generating|
|status|completed|
|status|failed|

<h2 id="tocS_TemplateRunStatus">TemplateRunStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematemplaterunstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_TemplateRunStatus"></a>
<a id="tocStemplaterunstatus"></a>
<a id="tocstemplaterunstatus"></a>

```json
"pending"
```

Where a run, or one of its outputs, is in its lifecycle. The run's is rolled
up from its outputs' (``aggregate_output_statuses``). A class rather than a
``Literal`` so it publishes as one named enum instead of being inlined into
every kind.

A `string` output, delivered as `content` once completed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The id of the generation behind this output. Pass it as a `generation` reference to use the output as an input elsewhere.|
|status|[TemplateRunStatus](#schematemplaterunstatus)|true|none|The lifecycle status of the output. It ends at `completed`, when the output's content fields are set, or `failed`, when `failure_reason` and `error_message` are set.|
|failure_reason|string \| null|false|none|The category of failure. Present only when `status` is `failed`.|
|error_message|string \| null|false|none|A human-readable description of the failure. Present only when `status` is `failed`. Failed generations are not charged.|
|type|string|true|none|The kind of output: the `type` of the port's `content_schema`.|
|content|string \| null|false|none|The generated text. Present only when `status` is `completed`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|generating|
|status|completed|
|status|failed|

A template the caller can run, and its runnable versions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Pass as `template_id` on `POST /v1/flows/templates/{template_id}/runs`.|

A version whose graph uses a model that is not available to you through the API is left out, as is one whose stored snapshot is gone; either way the list can be empty while the template still has versions the ElevenLabs app can run.|
|has_more_versions|boolean|true|none|Whether this template has further published versions beyond the `versions_per_template` returned here. Fetch `GET /v1/flows/templates/{template_id}` with a larger `versions_per_template` to see more of them.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The ID of the test invocation|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The user-provided name of the test invocation, if one was set.|
|agent_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the agent this test invocation belongs to|
|branch_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the branch this test invocation was run on|
|version_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the agent version this test invocation ran against. For draft or config-override runs this is the version those uncommitted changes were applied on top of. None only for runs recorded before this field existed.|
|ran_against_draft|boolean|false|none|Whether the run included uncommitted changes (a saved draft or an ad-hoc config override) layered on top of version_id.|
|runs_diverged_from_version|boolean|false|none|Whether the test runs in this invocation did not all execute against the same version, which happens when a subset of runs was resubmitted after the original run. When true, version_id describes the most recent resubmit rather than every run.|
|created_at_unix_secs|integer|true|none|Creation time of the test invocation in unix seconds|
|test_run_count|integer|true|none|Number of test runs in this invocation|
|passed_count|integer|true|none|Number of test runs that passed|
|failed_count|integer|true|none|Number of test runs that failed|
|pending_count|integer|true|none|Number of test runs that are pending|
|cancelled_count|integer|true|none|Number of test runs that were cancelled|
|title|string|true|none|Display title of the test invocation: the user-provided name when set, otherwise the folder name, single test name, or test count.|
|access_info|[ResourceAccessInfo](#schemaresourceaccessinfo) \| null|false|none|The access information of the test invocation|
|repeat_count|integer|false|none|Number of times each test was repeated in this invocation|
|cancelled|boolean|false|none|Whether this test invocation was cancelled|
|credits_used|integer \| null|false|none|Total credits billed across test runs in this invocation. None when no run has cost data.|
|total_price|number \| null|false|none|Total USD price across test runs in this invocation. None when no run has price data.|

<h2 id="tocS_ToDialogueSettingsResponseModel">ToDialogueSettingsResponseModel</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematodialoguesettingsresponsemodel"></a>

<a id="tocStodialoguesettingsresponsemodel"></a>
<a id="tocstodialoguesettingsresponsemodel"></a>

```json
{
  "stability": 0.5
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stability|number \| null|false|none|Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values introduce broader emotional range for the voice. Higher values can result in a monotonous voice with limited emotion.|
|similarity|number \| null|false|none|Determines how strongly the model is guided while generating. Higher values make the model adhere more closely to the voice, at the cost of variation. Not supported by every model.|
|clone_strength|number \| null|false|none|Controls how closely the voice matches the professional voice clone samples, from 0 (low) to 1 (high). We recommend 0 for most use cases. Increase this value only if you experience issues with the default settings. Only applies to professional voice clones fine-tuned for the selected v4 model.|

<h2 id="tocS_ToolAnnotations">ToolAnnotations</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematoolannotations"></a>
<a id="schema_ToolAnnotations"></a>
<a id="tocStoolannotations"></a>
<a id="tocstoolannotations"></a>

```json
{
  "title": "string",
  "readOnlyHint": true,
  "destructiveHint": true,
  "idempotentHint": true,
  "openWorldHint": true
}
```

Additional properties describing a Tool to clients.

NOTE: all properties in ToolAnnotations are **hints**.
They are not guaranteed to provide a faithful description of
tool behavior (including descriptive properties like `title`).

Clients should never make tool use decisions based on ToolAnnotations
received from untrusted servers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string \| null|false|none|none|
|readOnlyHint|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|destructiveHint|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|idempotentHint|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|openWorldHint|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
