<h2 id="tocS_TurnConfig">TurnConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematurnconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_TurnConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSturnconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsturnconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "interruption_ignore_term_languages": [],
  "interruption_ignore_terms": [],
  "merge_with_default_ignore_terms": false,
  "mode": "turn",
  "retranscribe_on_turn_timeout": false,
  "silence_end_call_timeout": -1,
  "soft_timeout_config": {
    "message": "Hhmmmm...yeah.",
    "timeout_seconds": -1
  },
  "speculative_turn": false,
  "spelling_patience": "auto",
  "transcribe_on_disabled_interruptions": false,
  "turn_eagerness": "normal",
  "turn_model": "turn_v3",
  "turn_timeout": 7
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|turn_timeout|number|false|none|Maximum wait time for the user's reply before re-engaging the user|
|initial_wait_time|number \| null|false|none|How long the agent will wait for the user to start the conversation if the first message is empty. If not set, uses the regular turn_timeout.|
|silence_end_call_timeout|number|false|none|Maximum wait time since the user last spoke before terminating the call|
|mode|[TurnMode](#schematurnmode)|false|none|The mode of turn detection|
|turn_eagerness|[TurnEagerness](#schematurneagerness)|false|none|Controls how eager the agent is to respond. Low = less eager (waits longer), Standard = default eagerness, High = more eager (responds sooner)|
|spelling_patience|[SpellingPatience](#schemaspellingpatience)|false|none|Controls if the agent should be more patient when user is spelling numbers and named entities. Auto = model based, Off = never wait extra|
|speculative_turn|boolean|false|none|When enabled, starts generating LLM responses during silence before full turn confidence is reached, reducing perceived latency. May increase LLM costs.|
|retranscribe_on_turn_timeout|boolean|false|none|When enabled, if VAD detects no speech, attempts to re-transcribe accumulated audio at turn timeout. Disables silence discount billing while enabled for the active agent or workflow node.|
|turn_model|[TurnModel](#schematurnmodel)|false|none|Version of the turn detection model to use.|
|interruption_ignore_terms|[string]|false|none|List of terms that should not trigger an interruption when spoken by the user (e.g. 'gotcha', 'understood'). Uses case-insensitive exact matching.|
|interruption_ignore_term_languages|[string]|false|none|Language codes for which preset ignore-term categories have been activated. Stored explicitly so display is not inferred from term overlap.|
|merge_with_default_ignore_terms|boolean|false|none|When enabled, the curated default terms for interruption_ignore_term_languages are used in addition to interruption_ignore_terms.|
|transcribe_on_disabled_interruptions|boolean|false|none|When interruptions are disabled, still transcribe what the user says so it can carry into the next turn. When off, user speech during a non-interruptible turn is ignored and won't trigger a turn.|
|soft_timeout_config|[SoftTimeoutConfig](#schemasofttimeoutconfig)|false|none|Configuration for soft timeout functionality. Provides immediate feedback during longer LLM responses.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|silence|
|mode|turn|
|turn_eagerness|patient|
|turn_eagerness|normal|
|turn_eagerness|eager|
|spelling_patience|auto|
|spelling_patience|off|
|turn_model|turn_v2|
|turn_model|turn_v3|


Which Twilio answering-machine-detection (AMD) mode to request for a call.

`enable` returns a verdict as soon as Twilio can tell a human from a machine.
`detect_message_end` additionally waits for the greeting to finish, which is what
distinguishes the `machine_end_*` verdicts, at the cost of a later result.

<h2 id="tocS_UUITransferConfig">UUITransferConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauuitransferconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_UUITransferConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSuuitransferconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsuuitransferconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "data": "string",
  "protocol_discriminator": "string",
  "protocol_discriminator_mode": "prefix"
}
```

User-to-User Information envelope for SIP REFER transfers (RFC 7433).

Outbound payloads are hex-encoded (the only encoding RFC 7433 defines). The
protocol discriminator axis lets per-platform formats (Talkdesk, Genesys, ...)
be expressed by configuration rather than scattered transfer flags. Further
axes (ASCII encoding, header name, purpose/content parameters) can be added
here without touching the transfer model.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|string|true|none|UUI payload to send on SIP REFER transfers. Supports inline dynamic variables and is hex-encoded at transfer time.|
|protocol_discriminator|string \| null|false|none|Optional one-octet protocol discriminator (two hex digits, e.g. '00'). Required by platforms such as Genesys Cloud, which otherwise strip the first octet of the payload. Leave unset for platforms like Talkdesk that expect a bare hex payload.|
|protocol_discriminator_mode|string|false|none|How to attach protocol_discriminator. 'prefix' prepends the octet to the hex payload (User-to-User=XX<hex>;encoding=hex). 'pd_parameter' sends it as a separate parameter (User-to-User=<hex>;pd=XX;encoding=hex). Ignored when protocol_discriminator is unset.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|protocol_discriminator_mode|prefix|
|protocol_discriminator_mode|pd_parameter|

<h2 id="tocS_VoiceDesignRequestModel">VoiceDesignRequestModel</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavoicedesignrequestmodel"></a>
<a id="schema_VoiceDesignRequestModel"></a>
<a id="tocSvoicedesignrequestmodel"></a>
<a id="tocsvoicedesignrequestmodel"></a>

```json
{
  "voice_description": "A sassy squeaky mouse",
  "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_ttv_v2",
  "text": "Every act of kindness, no matter how small, carries value and can make a difference, as no gesture of goodwill is ever wasted.",
  "auto_generate_text": false,
  "loudness": 0.5,
  "seed": 11,
  "guidance_scale": 5,
  "stream_previews": true,
  "should_enhance": true,
  "remixing_session_id": "123",
  "remixing_session_iteration_id": "123",
  "quality": 0.9,
  "reference_audio_base64": "string",
  "prompt_strength": 0.25
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice_description|string|true|none|Description to use for the created voice.|
|model_id|string|false|none|Model to use for the voice generation. Possible values: eleven_multilingual_ttv_v2, eleven_ttv_v3.|
|text|string \| null|false|none|Text to generate, text length has to be between 100 and 1000.|
|auto_generate_text|boolean|false|none|Whether to automatically generate a text suitable for the voice description.|
|loudness|number|false|none|Controls the volume level of the generated voice. -1 is quietest, 1 is loudest, 0 corresponds to roughly -24 LUFS.|
|seed|integer \| null|false|none|Random number that controls the voice generation. Same seed with same inputs produces same voice.|
|guidance_scale|number|false|none|Controls how closely the AI follows the prompt. Lower numbers give the AI more freedom to be creative, while higher numbers force it to stick more to the prompt. High numbers can cause voice to sound artificial or robotic. We recommend to use longer, more detailed prompts at lower Guidance Scale.|
|stream_previews|boolean|false|none|Determines whether the Text to Voice previews should be included in the response. If true, only the generated IDs will be returned which can then be streamed via the /v1/text-to-voice/:generated_voice_id/stream endpoint.|
|should_enhance|boolean|false|none|Whether to enhance the voice description using AI to add more detail and improve voice generation quality. When enabled, the system will automatically expand simple prompts into more detailed voice descriptions. Defaults to False|
|remixing_session_id|string \| null|false|none|The remixing session id.|
|remixing_session_iteration_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the remixing session iteration where these generations should be attached to. If not provided, a new iteration will be created.|
|quality|number \| null|false|none|Higher quality results in better voice output but less variety.|
|reference_audio_base64|string \| null|false|none|Reference audio to use for the voice generation. The audio should be base64 encoded. Only supported when using the  eleven_ttv_v3 model.|
|prompt_strength|number \| null|false|none|Controls the balance of prompt versus reference audio when generating voice samples. 0 means almost no prompt influence, 1 means almost no reference audio influence. Only supported when using the eleven_ttv_v3 model.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|model_id|eleven_multilingual_ttv_v2|
|model_id|eleven_ttv_v3|

<h2 id="tocS_VoiceSettingsResponseModel">VoiceSettingsResponseModel</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavoicesettingsresponsemodel"></a>

<a id="tocSvoicesettingsresponsemodel"></a>
<a id="tocsvoicesettingsresponsemodel"></a>

```json
{
  "similarity_boost": 1,
  "speed": 1,
  "stability": 1,
  "style": 0,
  "use_speaker_boost": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stability|number \| null|false|none|Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values introduce broader emotional range for the voice. Higher values can result in a monotonous voice with limited emotion.|
|use_speaker_boost|boolean \| null|false|none|This setting boosts the similarity to the original speaker. Using this setting requires a slightly higher computational load, which in turn increases latency.|
|similarity_boost|number \| null|false|none|Determines how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice when attempting to replicate it.|
|style|number \| null|false|none|Determines the style exaggeration of the voice. This setting attempts to amplify the style of the original speaker. It does consume additional computational resources and might increase latency if set to anything other than 0.|
|speed|number \| null|false|none|Adjusts the speed of the voice. A value of 1.0 is the default speed, while values less than 1.0 slow down the speech, and values greater than 1.0 speed it up.|
|clone_strength|number \| null|false|none|Controls how closely the voice matches the professional voice clone samples, from 0 (low) to 1 (high). We recommend 0 for most use cases. Increase this value only if you experience issues with the default settings. Only applies to professional voice clones fine-tuned for the selected v4 model.|

<h2 id="tocS_VoicemailDetectionToolConfig">VoicemailDetectionToolConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavoicemaildetectiontoolconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_VoicemailDetectionToolConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSvoicemaildetectiontoolconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsvoicemaildetectiontoolconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "system_tool_type": "voicemail_detection",
  "voicemail_message": "string"
}
```

Allows the agent to detect when a voicemail system is encountered.

This tool should be invoked by the LLM when it detects that the call has been
answered by a voicemail system rather than a human. If a voicemail message
is configured, it will be played; otherwise the call will end immediately.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|system_tool_type|string|false|none|none|
|voicemail_message|string \| null|false|none|Optional message to leave on voicemail when detected. If not provided, the call will end immediately when voicemail is detected. Supports dynamic variables (e.g., {{system__time}}, {{system__call_duration_secs}}, {{custom_variable}}).|

```json
{
  "response_timeout_secs": 20,
  "type": "webhook"
}
```

A webhook tool is a tool that calls an external webhook from our server

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of tool|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|description|string|true|none|Description of when the tool should be used and what it does.|
|response_timeout_secs|integer|false|none|The maximum time in seconds to wait for the tool call to complete. Must be between 5 and 300 seconds (inclusive).|
|disable_interruptions|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED: use `interruption_mode` instead. If true, the user will not be able to interrupt the agent while this tool is running.|
|interruption_mode|[ToolInterruptionMode](#schematoolinterruptionmode)|false|none|Controls whether the user can interrupt the agent around this tool call. 'allow' (default) lets the user interrupt at any time, 'disable_during_tool' suppresses interruptions only while the tool is running, 'disable_during_tool_and_turn' suppresses interruptions while the tool runs and for the agent response that follows it.|
|force_pre_tool_speech|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** DEPRECATED: use `pre_tool_speech` instead. If true, the agent will speak before the tool call.|
|pre_tool_speech|[PreToolSpeechMode](#schemapretoolspeechmode)|false|none|Controls whether the agent speaks before this tool is called. 'auto' (default) decides based on recent tool latency, 'force' always asks the agent to speak, 'off' fully opts out regardless of latency.|
|assignments|[[DynamicVariableAssignment](#schemadynamicvariableassignment)]|false|none|Configuration for extracting values from tool responses and assigning them to dynamic variables|
|tool_call_sound|[ToolCallSoundType](#schematoolcallsoundtype) \| null|false|none|Predefined tool call sound type to play during tool execution. If not specified, no tool call sound will be played.|
|tool_call_sound_behavior|[ToolCallSoundBehavior](#schematoolcallsoundbehavior)|false|none|Determines when the tool call sound should play. 'auto' only plays when there's pre-tool speech, 'always' plays for every tool call.|
|tool_error_handling_mode|[ToolErrorHandlingMode](#schematoolerrorhandlingmode)|false|none|Controls how tool errors are processed before being shared with the agent. 'auto' determines handling based on tool type (summarized for native integrations, hide for others), 'summarized' sends an LLM-generated summary, 'passthrough' sends the raw error, 'hide' does not share the error with the agent.|
|dynamic_variables|[DynamicVariablesConfig](#schemadynamicvariablesconfig)|false|none|Configuration for dynamic variables|
|execution_mode|[ToolExecutionMode](#schematoolexecutionmode)|false|none|Determines when and how the tool executes: 'immediate' executes the tool right away when requested by the LLM, 'post_tool_speech' waits for the agent to finish speaking before executing, 'async' runs the tool in the background without blocking - best for long-running operations.|
|api_schema|[WebhookToolApiSchemaConfig-Input](#schemawebhooktoolapischemaconfig-input)|true|none|The schema for the outgoing webhoook, including parameters and URL specification|
|follow_redirects|boolean|false|none|Whether to resolve a redirect from the endpoint and return the final response. One redirect is followed, as a GET without the request body; nothing configured on this tool (headers, authentication, client certificate) is sent to the redirect target. Both the endpoint and the redirect target must use HTTPS. Not supported for API integration tools.|
|follow_redirects_allowed_domains|[string]|false|none|Domains a redirect may point at, e.g. 'test.example.com'. Required when following redirects, and a target outside the list is refused.|

|interruption_mode|disable_during_tool|

|pre_tool_speech|off|

When disabled the caller hears silence until the transfer completes. SIP REFER transfers only.|
|uui|[UUITransferConfig](#schemauuitransferconfig) \| null|false|none|User-to-User Information (RFC 7433) to attach to SIP REFER transfers. Carries call context such as CRM identifiers or escalation reason across the transfer boundary.|

|type|string|false|none|none|
|position|[Position-Input](#schemaposition-input)|false|none|Position of the node in the workflow.|
|edge_order|[string]|false|none|The ids of outgoing edges in the order they should be evaluated.|

```json
    }
  ],
```

```json
  ],
```

```json
  "most_recent_failure_timestamp": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The display name for this webhook.|
|webhook_id|string|true|none|The unique ID for this webhook.|
|webhook_url|string|true|none|The HTTPS callback URL that is called when this webhook is triggered in the platform.|
|is_disabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the webhook has been manually disabled by a user.|
|is_auto_disabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the webhook has been automatically disabled due to repeated consecutive failures over a long period of time.|
|created_at_unix|integer|true|none|Original creation time of the webhook.|
|auth_type|[WebhookAuthMethodType](#schemawebhookauthmethodtype)|true|none|The authentication mode used to secure the webhook.|
|usage|[[WorkspaceWebhookUsageResponseModel](#schemaworkspacewebhookusageresponsemodel)] \| null|false|none|The list of products that are currently configured to trigger this webhook.|
|events|[[WorkspaceWebhookEventType](#schemaworkspacewebhookeventtype)] \| null|false|none|The workspace-level events this webhook is currently subscribed to. Only populated when usages are requested.|
|most_recent_failure_error_code|integer \| null|false|none|The most recent error code returned from the callback URL.|
|most_recent_failure_timestamp|integer \| null|false|none|The most recent time the webhook failed, failures are any non-200 codes returned by the callback URL.|
